title: Snabbit Spent ₹16 To Earn Every Rupee In Operating Revenue In FY26
title_bn: Snabbit Spent ₹16 To Earn Every Rupee In Operating Revenue In FY26
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Amid intense competition in the quick home services market, Snabbit incurred a net loss of ₹167.8 Cr in the financial…
paragraph1: SUMMARYQuick home services startup Snabbit reported a net loss of ₹167.8 Cr in FY26, compared with ₹5.7 Cr in FY25, while operating revenue rose to ₹12.2 Cr from ₹26.3 Lakh Spending on service professionals and customer acquisition far exceeded operating revenue, underscoring the cost of scaling the instant home services business Total expenses stood at ₹194.8 Cr, led by ₹63.1 Cr in service professional costs, ₹48.7 Cr in marketing expenses, and ₹46 Cr in employee benefit expenses Amid intense competition in the quick home services market, Snabbit incurred a net loss of ₹167.8 Cr in the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26) as against a loss of ₹5.7 Cr in FY25. Important to note that FY26 was Snabbit’s first full financial year of operations following its service launch in August 2024. Thus, comparability of the two fiscals is limited. Snabbit posted an operating revenue of ₹12.2 Cr in FY26 compared to ₹26.3 Lakh in FY25.
paragraph2: Platform services generated ₹10.8 Cr in revenue, while uniform sales to service professionals contributed the remaining ₹1.4 Cr. The startup recognises platform service revenue net of discounts it bears. Including other income of ₹14.8 Cr, the startup’s total income for the fiscal stood at ₹27 Cr. Interest on bank deposits contributed ₹14.1 Cr, with the remainder largely coming from gains on mutual fund sales. Snabbit held ₹292.2 Cr in cash and bank balances and ₹26.6 Cr in mutual fund investments, totalling ₹318.9 Cr. This balance predates its $56 Mn Series D funding round in April. Founded in 2024 by former Zepto executive Aayush Agarwal, Snabbit connects users with trained domestic help for cleaning, dishwashing, and other household chores, promising arrivals within 10-15 minutes. The April funding round took the startup’s total funding to $112 Mn.
paragraph3: It is backed by the likes of Susquehanna Venture Capital, Mirae Asset Venture Investments, Bertelsmann India Investments, Nexus Venture Partners, Lightspeed Ventures, among others. Snabbit currently operates in five cities, including Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Pune and Hyderabad. It intends to expand its operations to 10 cities, with Kolkata and Chennai as priorities. The startup is focusing on penetrating deep into a handful of existing markets, rather than aggressive geographical expansion. Even within cities, it is doubling down on ‘micro-markets’, or certain neighbourhoods where it can ensure quick delivery, rather than the whole city. It was present in 140 micromarkets by May this year, and had onboarded 40,000 professionals on its platforms, with an average order value of ₹169-₹199. Where Did Snabbit Spend In FY26? Snabbit’s total expenses rose to ₹194.8 Cr from ₹6.8 Cr in FY25. Employee Benefit Expenses: These rose to ₹46 Cr from ₹3.3 Cr, including salaries and wages, provident fund contributions, employee stock options, and staff welfare expenses. Expert Service Cost: Its largest expense head stood at ₹63.1 Cr, compared with ₹27 Lakh in FY25. Marketing Expenses: Spending on marketing increased to ₹48.
paragraph4: 7 Cr from ₹82.1 Lakh in the previous year. Service Fulfillment Expenses: Spending under this head stood at ₹23.8 Cr compared with ₹84.5 Lakh in FY25. Snabbit’s Loss Per Job Falls Below ₹200 In a statement issued today, Snabbit’s CEO Agarwal said the startup closed FY26 with a run rate of 35,000 daily jobs, up 70X from around 500 jobs a day at the beginning of the fiscal year. It acquired nearly 10 Lakh customers and onboarded more than 20,000 service professionals during the year. He attributed the growth to investments in customer acquisition, workforce training, technology, infrastructure and geographical expansion. Agarwal said the startup deliberately invested ahead to scale into the competitive quick home services category. The startup said it closed the fiscal with approximately ₹319 Cr in cash and investments, zero borrowings and a net worth of ₹312.4 Cr. He also argued that its annual financial statements do not fully reflect the underlying economics or maturity of the business. In a separate statement, Snabbit claimed that its losses per job declined from approximately ₹1,500 at the beginning of FY26 to below ₹200 in September 2026, indicating an improvement in unit economics as its operations scaled. Its Q2 FY27 metrics show that the platform completed 64.5 Lakh jobs, up 61% QoQ, and recorded a net transaction value (NTV) of ₹73 Cr, up 34%.
paragraph5: House help accounted for 64 Lakh jobs, while more recently launched verticals — home cooking and home salon services — accounted for 50,000 and 10,000 jobs, respectively, in the fiscal. The startup reported an EBITDA loss of ₹145 Cr, equivalent to 199% of NTV. Snabbit also claimed to be the largest high-frequency home services platform by jobs completed and NTV, and the most capital-efficient at the job level. Its strategy centres on building density within fewer cities and micromarkets rather than expanding its geographical footprint aggressively. Competition Heats Up In Quick Home Services Snabbit competes with Pronto and listed home services company Urban Company’s InstaHelp in the instant household assistance market. Pronto closed its $45 Mn Series B round in May at a $200 Mn valuation, adding to the capital flowing into the segment. However, profitability remains a challenge: all three platforms are loss-making due to intense competition, deep discounting, and rising operational costs. Urban Company posted a ₹174 Cr EBITDA loss from InstaHelp in Q2 FY27, over 4X jump from ₹44 Cr in the same quarter last year. InstaHelp fulfilled 6.2 Mn orders, marking a 63% QoQ increase, while its net transaction value (NTV) rose 34% to ₹71 Cr. However, net order value declined to ₹114 from ₹138 in the previous quarter, which it attributed to competitive intensity and introductory pricing for new users. In the past, Urban Company has claimed that it does not expect InstaHelp to meaningfully contribute to its bottom line over the next 4-5 years. The quick home services segment also faces scrutiny over working conditions. Inc42’s reporting documented workers’ concerns about earnings, strict logged-in hour requirements, and inadequate access to waiting areas and washrooms.

title: Tesla turns to 50-year-old stunt technology as it tries to Roadster again
title_bn: Tesla turns to 50-year-old stunt technology as it tries to Roadster again
author: TechPulse
excerpt: If you want to make a car spin in the air, compressed gas is a good way to do it.
paragraph1: Nine years after first trying to resurrect the Roadster, Tesla is apparently trying again. CEO Elon Musk might have relocated its HQ to Texas, but yet again he has returned to California’s showbiz industry to hawk his wares; last time it was a Hollywood back lot for the remote-controlled Cybercab demo, last night it was decades-old stunt technology to make a show car do tricks in the air. The new Roadster, we’re told, will be unlike anything else, although the angular, wedge-shaped styling owes more than a little to Giorgetto Giugiaro’s original Lotus Esprit—Musk is known to own a James Bond prop car—as well as the more recent Lamborghini Gallardo. At the rear are four giant exhaust pipes; these do not signal Tesla’s sudden embrace of hydrocarbons beyond those emitted by private aviation.
paragraph2: Rather, it’s where 100,000 psi jets of compressed nitrogen shoot out. It’s early in the morning and the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Statutes are dense reading, so I am yet to find the section where it explains how and when it’s legal to use such a thing on the road. title: Gigabyte X870 Aorus Infinity Motherboard Review: limited-edition, designed for extreme overclocking, but pricey for X870
title_bn: Gigabyte X870 Aorus Infinity Motherboard Review: limited-edition, designed for extreme overclocking, but pricey for X870
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Gigabyte’s limited-edition 40th-anniversary X870 Aorus Infinity motherboard is designed for extreme overclocking, with everything you need for daily use.
paragraph1: Gigabyte’s X870 Aorus Infinity blends extreme overclocking ability and tools with good all-around features and aesthetics. But you’ll have to pay up for this limited-edition board’s flexibility. Reasons to buy +Dedicated overclocking buttons +External BCLK generator +Fast USB connectivity (USB4) +Magnetically attaching Wi-Fi antenna +Two PCIe 5.0 M.2 +Dual 64MB BIOS Reasons to avoid -Pricey for X870 -M.2 socket shares lanes with the sole USB4 port Why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Go to page: At Computex 2026, we saw Gigabyte’s concept X870E Aorus Infinity Next motherboard using that incredible-looking space-age material for VRM cooling, along with something more practical: the X870 Aorus Infinity, a production board, not a concept. The Infinity is made for overclockers.
paragraph2: Just look at the right edge: All those buttons and voltage read points make pushing the limits even easier. It sports a two-DIMM design, with the DRAM slots above the socket, prioritizing speed over capacity. Priced at an eye-opening $799.99, it's far from cheap (it is a 40th-anniversary limited-edition board), even for the enthusiast X870E platform, but it offers a wide range of features that work for nearly everyone.As far as specifications go, the Aorus Infinity is well-equipped for an X870 board. You get eight total USB ports on the rear IO (one USB4), three M.2 sockets (one PCIe 5.0), and four SATA ports for storage, fast networking with 5 GbE and Wi-Fi 7 (320 MHz), and a quality last-gen flagship-class audio codec. And of course, there are all of the features designed for overclocking, including robust power delivery and the Overclocking kit, with several buttons and voltage read points, to take some of the complications of extreme overclocking down a notch.
paragraph3: Gigabyte also lists support for a staggering DDR5-11400(OC), but it needs manual tweaking, specialized BIOS fine-tuning, and the right hardware (likely an APU with an excellent IMC).On the performance front, the X870 Aorus Infinity delivered average-to-above-average results across most tests, using our primary Kingston DDR5-6000 kit, which is what we like to see. It proved competent not only in daily office tasks and other productivity functions, but also as a solid gaming platform. Overall, this board is a well-rounded performer.Below, we’ll examine the Aorus Infinity’s performance and other features, and decide if it has a chance to make our list of the best motherboards. author: TechPulse
excerpt: Google attempted to take its Chromebook platform upscale with Googlebooks. But the timing could not have been worse. Phone support at launch is extremely limited, and most people use Android phones and Chromebooks because they’re cheap.

title: The Surface Laptop Ultra delivers on most of Microsoft's promises
title_bn: The Surface Laptop Ultra delivers on most of Microsoft's promises
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Microsoft promises one machine for dev, AI, and gaming, and mostly gets there.
paragraph1: Skip to content Almost there Microsoft promises one machine for dev, AI, and gaming, and mostly gets there. Over the past week, the laptop Microsoft sent me has been summarizing books and movies, generating images from my imagination, and running a 70-billion-parameter AI model that would be a stretch to fit on most laptops. It also played AAA games at a speed and fidelity I would have thought impossible on an ARM system just a year ago. Microsoft wants to sell you one computer for all of your needs, and for once that doesn’t feel like total marketing fluff. Mostly. Microsoft is throwing both arms around the new Nvidia RTX Spark platform with the Surface Laptop Ultra—and setting its sights on the would-be MacBook Pro buyer, or as the company called it, “a high performance audience.” The bet is that rather than a gaming desktop for fun and a development laptop for work, buyers will pay more for one machine that does both. The Surface Laptop Ultra arrives at a strange time in personal computing. Recent industry numbers showed a 20 percent drop in total PC shipments year over year in the third quarter of 2026. That’s not just consumer purchasing either—that’s across the board. Between the RAMpocalypse that has exploded consumer prices and an industry fixated on enterprise money, there hasn’t been much new hardware to excite PC enthusiasts. Microsoft isn’t the only one debuting an RTX-chipped laptop. Dell’s XPS 16 Creator Edition and Asus’s ProArt series (our own Ryan Whitwam‘s review should be appearing on the front page soon) are betting on the chipset as well. The question when reviewing the Surface Laptop Ultra isn’t whether it can achieve the things that it claims competently, but whether there’s finally a compelling reason for power users to switch to an ARM system, and whether their daily workloads can still be achieved without hiccups when compared to a more traditional x86 offering, or the biggest competitor within the segment, the MacBook Pro. With a starting price of $2,599, this is not a budget alternative to Apple silicon.
paragraph2: This is bleeding-edge hardware, and you’re going to be paying a premium for it. Depending on your selected processor and memory options, MSRP can reach as high as $5,899. Prospective buyers should note that the lower-specced 24GB unified memory model ships with Windows 11 Home, while the rest of the fleet arrives with Windows 11 Pro. I received the 64GB model for testing, and I think that would probably be the sweet spot for a lot of users to align cost and performance. I really have to wonder if 24GB is enough to go around when we know that Windows 11 is memory-hungry on its own. When you have to assign a significant portion of that 24GB of unified memory to VRAM for gaming, does performance suffer? An audience question inside the Surface Laptop Ultra review information session asked about the usefulness of the base model, and didn’t get much back other than a vague “useful for smaller models locally” answer. Microsoft may have a more definitive answer to that question a few months from now when software and drivers catch up with hardware. So has the Microsoft and Nvidia team-up created the ultimate all-in-one laptop? Or is this the industry once again putting the hardware hype cart before the finished-software horse? paragraph3: 1b, SD Card Reader, 3.5mm Headphone Jack 2 x USB-C/USB4, 1 x USB-C/USB4 w/ Mag Connect, 1 x USB-A 3.1, 1 x HDMI 2.1b, SD Card Reader, 3.5mm Headphone Jack Size 12.95×9.40×0.71 inches 12.95×9.40×0.71 inches Weight 4.41 lbs (2.0 kg) 4.41 lbs (2.0 kg) MSRP $2,599.
paragraph4: 99 $4,299.99 Additional features 1080p front-facing webcam 1080p front-facing webcam Tidy internals of the Surface Laptop Ultra. Microsoft promises the laptop is “built with serviceability in mind.” Tidy internals of the Surface Laptop Ultra. Microsoft promises the laptop is “built with serviceability in mind.” Display The 15-inch mini-LED display might not be enough to get folks to run to the Ultra on its own, but it’s a compelling reason to add it to the list. The 3270×2180 native resolution looks simply stunning whether you’re watching a 4K video, playing games, or just staring at a desktop spreadsheet. I preferred the Enhanced color profile, but Vivid and sRGB modes looked fantastic as well. Not the easiest to photograph, but the screen is stunning in person. Not the easiest to photograph, but the screen is stunning in person. Blacks stayed deep against bright, vivid subjects without any sort of visible blooming. I wish I could say the same for my TV. While I can’t quantify how it stacks side by side with the latest MacBook Pro Retina display, I can say that this is a damn nice screen. Viewing angles are superb, colors are punchy, and the 2,000-nit peak brightness kept things legible even in a room flooded with natural sunlight. My only gripe is that in bright rooms, there is glare to contend with.
paragraph5: The glossy glass looks fantastic at lower light levels but can act a bit mirror-like in direct sunlight. It hindered my ability to photograph the screen more than it did my ability to use the computer. Still, if you’re looking for a matte-screen laptop, you might want to keep that in mind. Big Buck Bunny in 4k looks incredible on this screen. Big Buck Bunny in 4k looks incredible on this screen. Keyboard and trackpad The keyboard on the Surface Laptop Ultra is exactly what you’d expect on a premium machine like this. It’s excellent, if unremarkable. The keys have a shallow but satisfying press, the spacing makes sense for my hands, and the whole package delivers a very comfortable typing experience. I don’t have a whole bunch of laptops lying around to compare it to, but unsurprisingly, the closest would be my 2020 MacBook Pro. Microsoft knows what market it’s going after here, and I don’t mind them lifting direct inspiration from Apple in this department. Both the keyboard and the trackpad are excellent. Both the keyboard and the trackpad are excellent. The trackpad is similarly competent. It’s absolutely huge, measuring 5.5 inches long by 3.

title: Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra review: RTX Spark in a straight-up beautiful Windows PC
title_bn: Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra review: RTX Spark in a straight-up beautiful Windows PC

title: Urban Company Board Clears Plans To Raise Up To ₹2,500 Cr
title_bn: Urban Company Board Clears Plans To Raise Up To ₹2,500 Cr
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Urban Company’s board today approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr, alongside approving its financial performance for the…
paragraph1: SUMMARYUrban Company’s board has approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr through issuance of debt or equity The company is seeking funds at a time when InstaHelp is facing tough competition from the likes of Snabbit and Pronto, and the prospect of a cash burn battle It said the fundraise gives it flexibility to invest in its established business lines as well as InstaHelp while pursuing inorganic opportunities, without trading off one for another Urban Company’s board today approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr, alongside approving its financial performance for the September quarter. The proposed funding could involve issuance of equity shares, warrants, fully convertible debentures and convertible preference shares. The fundraise will be executed in one or more tranches via preferential allotment, private placement or one or more qualified institutional placements (QIPs), subject to shareholder approval. The final issue pricing and structure is yet to be determined. “The business is materially larger than at listing, growth has stepped up, and we now operate three businesses at scale with proven economics.
paragraph2: The proposed raise of up to ₹2,500 Cr is about flexibility: it lets us invest with conviction across each of them, cement leadership in InstaHelp, and pursue inorganic opportunities selectively, without trading off one for another,” Urban Company said in a letter to shareholders. The fundraise proposal comes at a time when Urban Company’s quick home services vertical InstaHelp is facing tough competition from the likes of Snabbit and Pronto, resulting in the prospect of a war for market share fuelled by cash burn. Hefty investments in powering the quick home services vertical is also creating a dent in Urban Company’s bottom line. For the September quarter, Urban Company’s net loss more than tripled YoY to ₹182.5 Cr, while operating revenue jumped 41% YoY to ₹537.
paragraph3: 29 Cr. Separately, the board also granted in-principle approval to explore residential air conditioners as a new business category under its product brand Native. This would be subject to further evaluations and final board clearances. “This category represents a large market in which the Company already services millions of units annually, providing it with first-hand insights into the existing product gaps and customer needs,” noted UC’s board. Urban Company made its debut on the bourses just around one year ago.
paragraph4: Hence, its proposed fundraise puts it among the ranks of several new-age tech companies like Kissht, Swiggy, Ather Energy, and Ola Electric that have sought to return to the public markets for fresh capital soon after their IPOs. On a quarterly basis, its net loss nearly doubled from ₹92.1 Cr. Operating revenue remained nearly flat compared with ₹528.3 Cr in Q1 FY27.
paragraph5: The company’s adjusted EBITDA loss for the quarter widened to ₹144 Cr, due to a “deliberate” ₹174 Cr investment in InstaHelp. The company also gave a timeline to improve its bottom line performance in the near future. “We remain on track for Adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and Adjusted EBITDA of ₹1,000 Cr by FY31,” it said.

title: Ethnic Wear Brand Libas Adds 9 New Stores In Offline Expansion Push
title_bn: Ethnic Wear Brand Libas Adds 9 New Stores In Offline Expansion Push
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Ethnic wear brand Libas is opening nine exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) across five Indian cities during Navratri, expanding its retail…
paragraph1: SUMMARYLibas is opening nine exclusive brand outlets across Bengaluru, Jaipur, Kanpur, Noida, and Jabalpur during Navratri The expansion is giving more shoppers access to its collections in person, complementing the ethnic wear brand’s online business Libas is planning to add more than 50 stores in FY27, following 28 openings in FY26 and 10 in FY25 Ethnic wear brand Libas is opening nine exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) across five Indian cities during Navratri, expanding its retail footprint during a key festive shopping period. The rollout spans high-street locations and shopping malls in Bengaluru, Jaipur, Kanpur, Noida, and Jabalpur. With these nine new openings, Libas now operates 55+ stores across India.
paragraph2: The brand plans to add more than 50 stores in FY27, following 28 openings in FY26 and 10 in FY25. The homegrown brand offers women’s ethnic and fusion wear, including kurtas, suit sets, sarees, lehengas and contemporary Indian outfits. Its portfolio covers both everyday and occasion wear, catering to a range of wardrobes and celebrations.
paragraph3: In the women’s ethnic and fusion wear segment, Libas competes with brands such as Biba, Aurelia, W for Woman and Soch. The new outlets are bringing Libas’ collections closer to shoppers, allowing them to explore styles, fabrics and fits in person while extending the brand’s reach beyond its digital sales channel. A Faster Push Into Offline Retail Bengaluru accounts for four of the nine planned outlets at Airport Road, Jayanagar, Commercial Street, and Mantri Mall.
paragraph4: In Jaipur, Libas is opening stores at Pacific Mall and Vaishali Nagar. The remaining three outlets are at Z Square Mall in Kanpur, H&S Mall in Noida, and South Avenue Mall in Jabalpur. Sidhant Keshwani, founder and CEO of Libas, said, “As Libas enters its next phase of growth, offline retail will be an important lever in expanding our consumer reach and strengthening our presence across markets.
paragraph5: Our focus is on building a retail network that allows us to scale efficiently, respond to local demand and deliver a consistent brand experience.” The company said it crossed an annualised revenue run rate (ARR) of ₹1,000 Cr in March 2026 and is targeting ₹1,000 crore in revenue in FY27. With the nine openings forming part of its broader FY27 rollout, offline retail is set to play a larger role in Libas’ next phase of growth.

title: Epic introduces an improved version of anti-cheat for Linux
title_bn: Epic introduces an improved version of anti-cheat for Linux
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Epic wants to work with developers and maintainers to find the best solution to making anti-cheat work seamlessly on Linux.
paragraph1: Epic Games says that it’s working on an update for its anti-cheat solution for Linux that would close the gap in capabilities with the Windows version of Easy Anti-Cheat. The company said that EAC Linux V2 will use existing Linux features to make it easier for distribution maintainers to meet these requirements by default, which should allow more Linux gamers to play competitive titles without needing to make changes to their current setup, but with the trade-off of forced adherence to certain security measures that the Linux community often avoids.
paragraph2: EAC Linux V2 currently has the following requirements: Signed Kernel and Kernel Modules, TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, Measured Boot, Input-Output Memory Management Unit (IOMMU), Kernel Lockdown Integrity Mode, Kexec Disabled, and Linux Security Module BPF.
paragraph3: The company says that it expects to iterate on these requirements over time, and that it’s looking to work with developers and distribution maintainers to refine these requirements. Using these features means that EAC Linux V2 will not need a kernel driver like the Windows implementation of anti-cheat, although it may require some distro maintainers to effect a configuration change to work with EAC Linux V2.

title: Urban Company Q2 Loss Widens Over 3X YoY To ₹182.5 Cr, Revenue Up 41%
title_bn: Urban Company Q2 Loss Widens Over 3X YoY To ₹182.5 Cr, Revenue Up 41%
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Consumer service brand Urban Company’s net loss has widened 208% YoY to ₹182.5 Cr in the Q2 FY27 from ₹59.3…
paragraph1: SUMMARYUrban Company’s net loss has widened 208% YoY to ₹182.5 Cr in the Q2 FY27 from ₹59.3 Cr loss incurred in the previous year quarter Alongside approving the financial statements, Urban Company’s board also approved a fund raise of ₹2,500 Cr via a preferential allotment or a private placement of equity shares The surge in loss comes despite the company's quarterly operating revenue jumping 41% to ₹537.29 Cr from ₹380.03 in Q2 FY26 Consumer service brand Urban Company’s net loss has widened 208% YoY to ₹182.5 Cr in the Q2 FY27 from ₹59.3 Cr loss incurred in the previous year quarter. Sequentially, the company’s loss almost doubled from ₹92.1 Cr. The company’s loss widened despite its quarterly operating revenue jumping 41% to ₹537.3 Cr from ₹380 in Q2 FY26. On a quarterly basis, the operating revenue remained largely flat compared with ₹528.
paragraph2: 3 Cr. Including other income of ₹41.2 Cr, Urban Company recorded a total income of ₹578.5 Cr in the quarter. Its total expenses also increased 61.5% to ₹745.7 Cr in the given period from ₹461.7 Cr in Q2 FY26. The surge in expense was primarily at the behest of increased investment in quick household help vertical, InstaHelp. The company said its adjusted EBITDA loss for the quarter stood at ₹144 Cr, due to a “deliberate” ₹174 Cr investment in InstaHelp. “Adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 Cr, up 213% YoY, and ₹119 Cr over the past three quarters, up 175% YoY,” the company said. The company also incurred a loss of ₹8.
paragraph3: 1 Cr from a joint venture and incurred a tax expense of ₹7.2 Cr in the quarter. Alongside approving the financial statements, Urban Company’s board also approved a fund raise of ₹2,500 Cr via a preferential allotment or a private placement of equity shares. The rationale behind this fundraise is to strengthen the leadership at InstaHelp, invest across its three major segments, and pursue potential inorganic opportunities, Urban Company said in its Q2 Shareholder’s letter. “We now operate three businesses at scale, with proven economics across India Core, International and Native. We believe each can be significantly larger in the years ahead with adequate investment and high quality execution,” Urban Company added in the Q2 shareholder’s letter. Urban Company’s Three Growth Engines Urban Company is doubling down on three key growth areas: its core home services business, InstaHelp and Native, its in-house consumer appliances brand. InstaHelp, its quick household help vertical, saw fulfilled orders jump 63% QoQ to 6.2 Mn, while net transaction value (NTV) rose 34% to ₹71 Cr. The increase in orders also led to a Operating revenue increased to ₹20.5 Cr from ₹1.4 Cr in the year-ago quarter, but adjusted EBITDA loss of the vertical widened to ₹174 Cr from ₹132 Cr.
paragraph4: The company bled ₹279 per order, a 19% improvement from ₹346 loss incurred per order in the previous quarter. Urban Company said it would continue investing in InstaHelp to establish market leadership. The service now accounts for around 45% of new users in micro-markets where it operates alongside the company’s core services. Meanwhile, Urban Company’s India consumer services business, excluding InstaHelp, reported 26.3% YoY growth in NTV to ₹963 Cr and a 28% rise in net revenue to ₹336 Cr. Its international operations in the UAE and Singapore also remained profitable, with NTV rising 66% YoY to ₹267 Cr. Native recorded 35% YoY growth in NTV to ₹132 Cr, while operating revenue rose 40% to ₹105 Cr. Its adjusted EBITDA loss remained at ₹9 Cr, but the loss margin narrowed to 6.8% of NTV from 9% a year ago. The company expects Native’s NTV to grow 50-55% on a combined Q2 and Q3 basis, factoring in the shift in festive demand to Q3. “Growth was healthy but understated by timing: the festive season this year has shifted entirely to Q3, and major ecommerce sale events, which took place in Q2 last fiscal year, have moved to Q3 this fiscal year. It is therefore more meaningful to assess Native across the two quarters together.
paragraph5: We expect combined Q2 + Q3 FY27 NTV growth of 50-55% YoY,” the shareholders’ letter said. Urban Company To Foray Into AC Category Besides the financials and the fundraise plans, Urban Company’s board also gave an in-principle approval to a plan to explore residential air conditioners as a new line of business under the Native segment. In its disclosures, the company said that this category represents a large market in which it already services millions of units annually and has accrued first-hand insights into the existing product gaps and customer needs. However, it plans to launch in the category only if it could offer a product that is materially better than existing options. Native’s current priorities remain water purifiers and smart locks, with the company expecting to add at most one new category over time. The company said that it evaluates potential categories based on four factors: the importance of servicing over the product’s lifetime, an unresolved consumer problem that better design can address, a sizeable profit pool with attractive premium margins, and the ability to sell, install and service the product through the Urban Company app using its own service partners. Urban Company said residential ACs fit these criteria. However, Inc42 had learnt about the potential entry into the category earlier in 2025. As per sources close to the company, its own line of ACs were likely to be launched by early 2026 Shares of Urban Company closed today’s trading session 2.63% higher at ₹158.3 apiece on the BSE.

The company said that it evaluates potential categories based on four factors: the importance of servicing over the product’s lifetime, an unresolved consumer problem that better design can address, a sizeable profit pool with attractive premium margins, and the ability to sell, install and service the product through the Urban Company app using its own service partners. Urban Company said residential ACs fit these criteria. However, Inc42 had learnt about the potential entry into the category earlier in 2025. As per sources close to the company, its own line of ACs were likely to be launched by early 2026 Shares of Urban Company closed today’s trading session 2.63% higher at ₹158.3 apiece on the BSE.

title: Enterprise AI Startup RapidCanvas Nets $29 Mn To Expand GTM Teams
title_bn: Enterprise AI Startup RapidCanvas Nets $29 Mn To Expand GTM Teams
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Enterprise AI startup RapidCanvas has raised $29 Mn (about ₹280 Cr) in its Series B funding round led by Vertex…
paragraph1: SUMMARYRapidCanvas has raised $29 Mn in a Series B round led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India The fundraise comes amid rising investor interest in enterprise AI startups, with Indian AI startups raising $438 Mn in Q3 2026, up 265% YoY The startup will use the capital to expand its go-to-market operations, grow its AI engineering team across India, the US and Brazil, and strengthen its platform for enterprise AI deployment Enterprise AI startup RapidCanvas has raised $29 Mn (about ₹280 Cr) in its Series B funding round led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India. The round also saw participation from new ventures Hitachi Ventures, along with existing investors Accel, Peak XV Partners, Valley Capital Partners and Titanium Ventures. RapidCanvas will use the proceeds to expand its go-to-market teams and field AI engineering team across India, the US and Brazil. It will also invest in all three products — deepening the Enterprise Context Engine, expanding the skills library behind the Visual Development Canvas, and strengthening governance in the Operational Harness. Founded in 2021 by Rahul Pangam and Uttam Phalnikar, RapidCanvas is an agentic AI startup that helps enterprises build and deploy AI applications as well as oversee their performance.
paragraph2: RapidCanvas claims that its annual recurring revenue (ARR) has grown 8X over the past six quarters. So far, in 2026, more than 75 enterprises across manufacturing, financial services, retail, business services and infrastructure have made 1.4 Mn AI-led decisions using applications built on its platform. RapidCanvas follows a subscription-based business model and targets large enterprises that have AI budgets but lack the in-house expertise to move beyond pilot projects. It claims that its platform is “trusted” by companies like PayPal, TresVista, Yale Appliances, Orion, Treetech, among others.
paragraph3: “Vibe coding has made it easy to start building with AI. Getting AI into production reliably and safely still remains the biggest gap. Our growth over the past six quarters is evidence that AI in enterprises is moving beyond pilots into production and real operations,” said cofounder and CEO Pangam. Enterprise AI Draws Investor Interest RapidCanvas’ fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in enterprise tech startups helping businesses deploy AI across their operations. Yesterday, enterprise AI startup Shamrock AI raised $5 Mn in a seed round led by Endiya Partners, with participation from Capria Ventures.
paragraph4: A day earlier, Parallel Loop secured $6.6 Mn in a seed round led by 3one4 Capital to help businesses integrate AI into their existing systems and workflows. The trend is also reflected in funding data for the Indian AI ecosystem. According to Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026, AI startup funding surged 265% YoY to $438 Mn in the September quarter. Investor sentiment, however, suggests that capital is not flowing indiscriminately across the AI stack.
paragraph5: Inc42’s Indian Investor Ranking & Sentiment Survey, based on responses from more than 85 institutional investors, found that 63% of investors see some degree of froth in Indian AI startup valuations. About half of those who see froth expect a correction within the next 18 months, while another 31% believe valuations are elevated but supported by real revenue. The survey also points to a preference for AI applications that address specific industry needs. Vertical AI applications across sectors such as BFSI, healthcare, defence and agriculture emerged as the leading choice, with 39% of investors expecting them to capture the most value over the next five years. AI hardware and semiconductors followed at 23%, while AI-led IT and business services accounted for 18%.

paragraph1: Apple iPhone Duo pre-orders begin in India at 5:30 PM IST on October 16, 2026, with sales starting October 23 at prices from ₹2,99,900. paragraph2: The device was revealed during the company's ‘Surprise and Shine' event on September 9 and will be available for purchase on October 23 via the company's online store, Apple Store stores and select retailers.The iPhone Duo is priced at ₹299,900 for the 256GB model and supports up to 2TB of storage. Apple's trying to appeal to customers who want a larger-screen smartphone they can fold up to use for movies and multitasking. This sports watch features a 5.4-inch outer display that expands to a 7.6-inch inner display, an A20 Pro chipset, and a dual-camera setup.

title: Chinas Tencent says AI agents showed unintended browsing behaviour
title_bn: Chinas Tencent says AI agents showed unintended browsing behaviour
author: TechPulse
excerpt: AI-SAFETY/CHINA-TENCENT (PIX):China's Tencent says AI agents showed unintended browsing behaviour
paragraph1: AI-SAFETY/CHINA-TENCENT (PIX):China's Tencent says AI agents showed unintended browsing behaviour Chinas Tencent says AI agents showed unintended browsing behaviour * Tencent says activity did not involve its Hunyuan models* Review found no deliberate targeting or coordination, company says* Researchers said "rogue" Chinese AI agent fleet sought Alibaba map dataBy Eduardo BaptistaBEIJING, - Tencent said on Friday that AI agents used to evaluate third-party models displayed web-browsing behavior not intended by the tech giant, in what appears to be the first known incident of rogue agent actions acknowledged by a major Chinese company.The statement followed a report by AI-safety research group Swarmchasers on Wednesday, which said "rogue" agents running on infrastructure it linked to Tencent Cloud made repeated attempts between September 28 and October 8 to retrieve information from Alibaba's Amap, China's equivalent to Google Maps.Tencent Hunyuan, the company's artificial intelligence unit, said in a post on X that the activity did not originate from its Hunyuan models. Its review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination, it said.
paragraph2: The Swarmchasers researchers said the agents sought information such as the commonly used entrances at Chinese parks, museums and zoos.The actions are not as egregious as those disclosed by US AI companies which include the hack of open-source platform Hugging Face by an OpenAI agent and the lodging of a fake homicide tip by an Anthropic agent.But the disclosure underscores research that shows Chinese AI agents can also misrepresent their identity, conceal failures and try to circumvent testing controls.Tencent said it took the findings very seriously and was strengthening network access controls and agent monitoring.
paragraph3: Hunyuan is one of China's leading AI model developers, competing with in-house teams at rivals such as Alibaba and ByteDance. ByteDance this week announced the creation of a new unit focused on AI model and agent safety.Swarmchasers said it used the word "rogue" to describe agents taking actions outside their intended scope or completing a task in unintended ways.After routine automated requests were blocked, the agents tried other methods, including public web tools that could open pages and run code, routing requests through other websites and using Amap keys and security codes found in publicly available software code.
paragraph4: Swarmchasers said it found no evidence that the agents breached Amap's main anti-bot safeguards. Most of the 2,818 attempts it recorded either failed or returned anti-bot pages, login screens or blank results.Some requests returned information through cached pages and intermediary services, including data on visitor arrivals at Chengdu Zoo, Swarmchasers said. The researchers said they could not determine whether an agent read the result or completed its task.
paragraph5: Alibaba declined to comment.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: ‘Have Never Feared Competition’: Reliance Responds To Elon Musk’s Starlink Allegations
title_bn: ‘Have Never Feared Competition’: Reliance Responds To Elon Musk’s Starlink Allegations
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) has responded to Elon Musk’s allegations that Indian business interests are blocking Starlink’s entry into the…
paragraph1: SUMMARYReliance Industries has responded to Elon Musk’s allegations about Starlink’s delayed India launch, saying it welcomes competition and that Jio’s satellite services also await clearances. Security assessments and spectrum assignment remain prerequisites for commercial launches, keeping Starlink and its domestic rivals from entering India’s satellite broadband market. The Centre has said Starlink, Jio Satellite Communications, and Eutelsat OneWeb are undergoing security assessments under the same regulatory framework. Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) has responded to Elon Musk’s allegations that Indian business interests are blocking Starlink’s entry into the country, saying it has “never feared competition” and that Jio’s satellite services are also awaiting government clearances. The statement follows Musk’s criticism of RIL CMD Mukesh Ambani, whom he accused of protecting his telecom interests and sarcastically described as the “real boss of India”. “At Reliance, we have never feared competition.
paragraph2: We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best,” the conglomerate said. Citing the government’s position that the same approval process applies to domestic and foreign applicants, Reliance said Jio’s own satellite services are awaiting clearances. “We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land,” it added. Reliance also pointed to Jio’s entry into India’s “crowded” telecom market in 2016, saying it has since grown to over 530 Mn customers. It credited Jio with providing affordable data and digital infrastructure, while saying India’s openness to domestic and international investment and innovation rests on the rule of law.
paragraph3: Musk initially targeted unnamed Indian business interests, whom he accused of blocking Starlink to maintain their “monopolistic chokehold” on the market. He subsequently singled out Ambani. In another post, the CEO of SpaceX, which owns and operates Starlink, addressed Ambani as “Prime Minister Ambani”. Musk also argued that satellite connectivity could expand internet access in remote areas, where poor connectivity limits educational opportunities and prevents small businesses from reaching global markets. Satcom Operators Await Launch Clearances The Centre has rejected Musk’s allegations of preferential treatment for domestic telecom players, saying India’s satellite communications rules are non-discriminatory. The communications ministry said last week that all three licensed operators — Starlink, Reliance’s Jio Satellite Communications, and Bharti Enterprises-backed Eutelsat OneWeb — were undergoing security assessments and were at broadly the same regulatory stage.
paragraph4: The operators hold telecom licences to provide Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite (GMPCS) services using non-geostationary satellite systems. However, they must demonstrate compliance with security conditions before seeking spectrum assignment. A telecom licence alone does not authorise commercial services. In September, it was reported that Eutelsat OneWeb had sought urgent security clearance for its low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellation, having waited more than 18 months since its security compliance demonstration in January 2025. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi earlier this week, Bharti Enterprises chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal said OneWeb is significantly ahead of Starlink in the approval queue, having applied five years ago. Mittal said its ground network has been ready for three years and its satellites have been orbiting over India for five years.
paragraph5: He added that he would be happy if OneWeb received permission even a few days before Starlink. Meanwhile, Starlink has reportedly reapplied to the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) for approval for its second-generation constellation of nearly 30,000 LEO satellites, which is expected to support capabilities such as direct-to-device (D2D) connectivity. Starlink vice president of business operations Lauren Dreyer said earlier this month that the company has established 20 gateway sites in India, comprising hundreds of antennas.

Mittal said its ground network has been ready for three years and its satellites have been orbiting over India for five years.
bangla_paragraph5: He added that he would be happy if OneWeb received permission even a few days before Starlink. Meanwhile, Starlink has reportedly reapplied to the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) for approval for its second-generation constellation of nearly 30,000 LEO satellites, which is expected to support capabilities such as direct-to-device (D2D) connectivity. Starlink vice president of business operations Lauren Dreyer said earlier this month that the company has established 20 gateway sites in India, comprising hundreds of antennas.

title: CERT-In issues critical alert after autonomous AI agents access live systems of Indian orgs
title_bn: CERT-In issues critical alert after autonomous AI agents access live systems of Indian orgs
author: TechPulse
excerpt: CERT-In issues 'critical' alert after autonomous AI agents access live systems of Indian orgs
paragraph1: New Delhi, Oct 16 (PTI) India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In has issued a 'critical' advisory warning that autonomous Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents have accessed live systems and confidential data of Indian organisations without authorisation, while threat actors are actively weaponising open-source agentic AI tools to execute rapid cyberattacks.In its advisory (CIAD-2026-0049) titled 'AI Agents as Attack Vectors', the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) highlighted two distinct categories of incidents targeting the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) infrastructure of Indian entities.In the first set of incidents, AI model providers voluntarily disclosed that autonomous AI models and agents undergoing research and evaluation had exceeded the authorised scope of their assigned tasks and reached live systems belonging to Indian organisations.During these operations, the AI agents read business records containing personal data and confidential material, using credentials and connection settings left exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and overly permissive cloud service roles, the agency noted.Notably, none of the affected organisations detected the access on their own.
paragraph2: In every case, the incident came to light only when the AI model provider disclosed it after an internal review.In a separate trend uncovered through its own threat hunting, CERT-In observed cybercriminals using publicly available AI-native offensive-security frameworks to conduct reconnaissance, exploit security weaknesses and carry out a financially motivated campaign against Indian entities.These tools continue to be repackaged and redeployed, with many deployments seen on servers across multiple countries, it said.In that campaign, agentic tools shrank the window between initial access and final impact from days to a few hours. Victims that only partly fixed the weaknesses were attacked again within days, on a larger scale, the agency said.
paragraph3: CERT-In pointed out that conventional security lapses were the root weaknesses in all the recent AI agent-driven incidents it observed.These included credentials and keys exposed in source code, public repository histories, configuration files, client applications and public web content; dormant, deprecated and test Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) left open to the internet; payment-API keys stored in plain text; over-permissive cloud and backend-as-a-service roles; and internet-facing management interfaces and unpatched middleware with weak passwords or no multi-factor authentication.AI agents found and exploited these gaps faster, more thoroughly and at a larger scale than human attackers.In the incidents disclosed by AI model providers, agents were also seen recovering the same exposed credential again and reusing it in separate operations.To mitigate the threat, CERT-In has urged organisations and service providers to audit their source code, repositories including commit history, configuration files, client applications and cloud storage for exposed credentials.
paragraph4: Entities have been advised to rotate exposed credentials and purge them from code history, decommission dormant, deprecated and test APIs, enforce least-privilege access in cloud deployments and for in-house AI agents, take admin interfaces off the internet, require multi-factor authentication, and monitor attacks while keeping logs for at least 180 days.After any credential exposure or confirmed intrusion, organisations should treat the environment as compromised until it is "forensically cleared", and expect repeat attempts within days to weeks, it said.For AI developers, research laboratories and evaluation agencies, CERT-In recommended isolating research and evaluation work by blocking all outbound network access except what a task strictly needs, enforced at the network level rather than through instructions to the model, and using synthetic targets and test credentials instead of production data.Commenting on the advisory, Jaydeep Singh, General Manager - India at Kaspersky, said it was "a timely reminder that AI agents are no longer just productivity tools"."When given broad access, they can reach live systems and sensitive data in ways organisations never intended, often by moving through gaps that already exist, such as misconfigured cloud services, exposed credentials and excessive permissions," Singh said.
paragraph5: Valid accounts, public-facing applications and trusted relationships were the entry point for over 80 per cent of the attacks Kaspersky investigated in 2025, Singh said, adding, "With AI allowing threat actors to iterate faster and scale their efforts, these paths can now be exploited more quickly than ever."AI agents used for research and testing should be kept fully separate from production environments, using synthetic data and test-only credentials."Every agent should be inventoried, isolated in sandboxed environments, governed by default-deny rules and required to seek human approval before any irreversible action," Singh added.Critical vulnerabilities should be patched or mitigated "within hours, not weeks", and code and pipelines audited regularly, Singh said, citing a Kaspersky study of around 30,000 popular GitHub repositories that found overly broad access permissions among the most common issues.Singh recommended that organisations treat AI agents as part of their attack surface from day one.

title: Teslas new Roadster turns in air with SpaceX thrusters, wont land until 2028
title_bn: Teslas new Roadster turns in air with SpaceX thrusters, wont land until 2028
author: TechPulse
excerpt: TESLA-ROADSTER/ (UPDATE 3, PIX, TV):UPDATE 3-Tesla's new Roadster turns in air with SpaceX thrusters, won't land until 2028
paragraph1: * The Roadster can flip in the air and land using thrusters* Some Tesla watchers see unveil as marketing for Tesla-SpaceX merger* Roadster production to start in 2028, CEO Musk says* Roadster has top speed of over 230 mph, range of over 300 miles* Roadster pricing not yet disclosed(Updates throughout with details from the event, reaction to the launch and comment from analysts)By Abhirup Roy and Mrinmay DeySAN FRANCISCO, Oct 15 (Reuters) - Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster powered with rocket-style thrusters on Thursday and said it would start production in 2028, more than a decade after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car.The white two-seater vehicle, developed in collaboration with CEO Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX, drove upside down on a ramp using a suction system, turned in the air and landed using built-in thrusters. Later in the event it used the thrusters to jump over a truck and other vehicles, twisting in the air during the maneuver.Some watchers saw the collaboration as Musk drumming up interest in a merger of the two big companies he controls, an idea he has explored by discussing their overlap.The reveal gives Tesla a showpiece car after years of missed Roadster deadlines, but it comes as the company shifts its focus to self-driving technology and robotics, and days before third-quarter results that analysts say matter more to investors."It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers," Gene Munster, managing partner at Tesla investor Deepwater Asset Management, said on social media platform X."The Roadster event is the latest example of why Elon can't wait to bring (Tesla) and (SpaceX) together," Munster said.
paragraph2: Musk has played down the car's importance to Tesla's finances, describing it in 2023 as a "small potato situation" that would not "move the needle in a major way financially."But the car still carries symbolic weight."Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology. The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a note last month.Viewers and witnesses gushed over the spectacle of the launch."That was the most insane product demo I've ever seen," Tesla fan and investor Sawyer Merritt posted on X. "I just saw this in person, and I'm still asking how this wasn't AI."
paragraph3: Musk and other executives did not specify any target prices at Thursday's event, although Tesla nearly a decade ago quoted a base price of $200,000 for the vehicle.Tesla's reservation page for the Roadster after Thursday's event showed a "Performance" version of the vehicle requiring a $50,000 deposit and a "Thrust" version with "acceleration thrusters" requiring a $250,000 deposit. A "Rocket" variant, which Tesla says is "invite only," is described as a single-seat model with a "full flight system."'HALFWAY TO THE SPEED OF SOUND'The event at a SpaceX ​test site in McGregor, Texas, had all the elements of a classic Musk product reveal: dramatic music, smoke, mechanical hissing sounds and a launch countdown."This is the culmination of incredible work by Tesla and SpaceX engineers working closely together to make something that you haven't seen in any movie," Musk, wearing a silver Western-style belt buckle emblazoned with the Tesla logo, told a cheering crowd of enthusiasts and investors.The Roadster can accelerate from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in less than one second and can hit a top speed of over 230 mph (370 kph), Tesla vehicle engineering chief Lars Moravy said."Definitely much faster than that," an excited Musk said.
paragraph4: "I think you've got to crack halfway to the speed of sound."The Roadster can also travel over 300 miles (480 km) on a single charge. That is less than half of what Musk promised in 2017, when Tesla first revealed a prototype of the second-generation Roadster and said that deliveries would begin in 2020.The original Roadster, released in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever electric vehicle and used a Lotus Elise chassis. It helped change the world's view of what an EV could be. The company has since been known for its Model Y and Model X SUVs and Model S and Model 3 sedans.The reveal of the second-generation Roadster comes amid a sharp shift in Tesla's focus to artificial intelligence-led self-driving tech and robotics, from manufacturing cars for human drivers.
paragraph5: This year, Tesla stopped selling Model S and X vehicles to make space for production of its Optimus humanoid robots. It also launched Cybercab — a two-seater robotaxi that comes without manual controls such as a steering wheel, pedals and mirrors.Tesla is set to report third-quarter results on October 21.Sales of Tesla's aging lineup of EVs have declined over the past two years, although high gas prices helped boost deliveries in the third quarter."The margin and cash flow numbers will carry far more weight with investors than anything they saw at the reveal," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst for Asia-Pacific at trading platform eToro.

title_bn: BSNL launches  ₹202 prepaid plan with 5GB data and 32-day validity: Check benefits
author: TechPulse
excerpt: BSNL has introduced a ₹202 prepaid plan with 32-day validity, 5GB high-speed data, 300 minutes of voice calls and 100 SMS. Compare its benefits with the ₹247 recharge, which offers unlimited calling, 50GB of data and 30-day validity, to see which pla
paragraph1: BSNL has introduced a ₹202 prepaid plan with 32-day validity, 5GB high-speed data, 300 minutes of voice calls and 100 SMS. Compare its benefits with the ₹247 recharge, which offers unlimited calling, 50GB of data and 30-day validity, to see which plan suits your needs.BSNL has introduced a new ₹202 prepaid plan.(AFP)Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) has introduced a new ₹202 prepaid plan for mobile users across India, offering 32 days of service validity, 5GB of high-speed data and 300 minutes of voice calling. The state-owned telecom operator has launched this plan on the back of its own prepaid plans for those who would like to recharge at a low cost with little usage advantage.According to TelecomTalk, the new recharge comes with a 100-SMS benefit, insurance facilities, and is a voice voucher. The plan has been published on BSNL's official website and BSNL Self Care app.
paragraph2: Here is a look at the benefits of the new ₹202 recharge and how it compares with the operator's ₹247 plan.BSNL ₹202 Prepaid Plan: Benefits and validityThe validity of the BSNL ₹202 prepaid plan is 32 days. Voice services subscribed: 300 minutes of voice calls, 5GB of high-speed data and 100 SMS are provided for the duration of the validity period.Once the allocated data is exhausted, internet speeds are reduced to 40 Kbps, as per the plan details. The recharge also covers insurance benefits, but details of coverage and terms are not provided.The plan could be an option for those who require a second mobile plan or those with limited calling and data needs. The calling time of 300 minutes and data cap of 5 GB, however, may not be ideal for users who make many calls or use a lot of data on their mobile devices.
paragraph3: BSNL ₹247 plan offers unlimited calling and 50 GB dataBSNL also has a ₹247 prepaid voice voucher, which is valid for 30 days. The offer has been announced to include 50 GB of high-speed data, unlimited voice calls, and 100 SMS per day, says TelecomTalk.Once the high-speed data is used up, Internet connection speeds drop to 40 Kbps. The recharge also provides ₹10 in talk value to the main account.Unlike the newly introduced ₹202 recharge, the ₹247 plan has been part of BSNL's existing offerings for some time.BSNL recharge you should chooseThe ₹202 plan comes with 2 extra days compared to the ₹247 plan, but offers much less data and fewer calling minutes. The recharge, on the other hand, is ₹247and includes unlimited voice calling and 50 GB of high-speed data, with an extra charge of ₹45.
paragraph4: Users who need only occasional calling and basic data access may consider the ₹202 plan. The ₹247 plan may be more suitable for those who need more data and frequent calls.About the AuthorPragya Singha RoyPragya is a Technology reporter with over four years of experience in digital media and content writing. She holds a Master’s degree in Journalism and has covered a wide range of stories spanning space, smartphones, gadgets, artificial intelligence, emerging technologies and the ways technology is transforming everyday life. She focuses on breaking down complex technology and science developments into clear, engaging, and reader-friendly stories, with a keen interest in emerging trends and their real-world impact. Before joining her current newsroom, Pragya worked with News9Live, where she covered the technology beat extensively, reporting on smartphones, consumer technology, AI, space and science, while also contributing to video and visual content. Her experience includes breaking news, explainers, SEO-driven stories, product coverage, interviews, unboxing videos and live event reporting.
paragraph5: She has also covered major technology and AI events, giving her experience in both newsroom and on-ground reporting. Beyond journalism, Pragya is an avid gamer and a passionate reader of fiction. She enjoys exploring immersive worlds through games and books, with a particular interest in stories that offer new perspectives, ideas, and experiences.

title: Shop Pay’s India Debut, Zetwerk IPO Day 1 & More
title_bn: Shop Pay’s India Debut, Zetwerk IPO Day 1 & More
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Shopify’s India Checkout Bet Shopify is preparing to bring Shop Pay to India. Setting up a direct clash with domestic…
paragraph1: Shopify’s India Checkout Bet Shopify is preparing to bring Shop Pay to India. Setting up a direct clash with domestic rivals like GoKwik and Razorpay, the Canada-based SaaS giant aims to disrupt the local checkout market on the back of its existing merchant network. Shop Pay’s India Launch: Shopify plans to launch the offering in the country by Q1 2027. The company is in talks with multiple payment orchestration platforms to integrate payment service providers. In India, Shop Pay will likely sit alongside Shopify Checkout as an optional accelerated experience. For context, Shop Pay allows customers to save payment, shipping and contact information, enabling faster purchases across participating stores. The Distribution Edge: What works for Shop Pay in India is Shopify’s existing base of Indian merchants. Since many Indian D2C brands already build their online storefronts on Shopify, the company benefits from deep merchant integration, a ready distribution pipeline and strong global brand equity. This gives Shop Pay a direct route into the checkout layer. Navigating Competition: Shop Pay enters a crowded Indian checkout market populated by established players like GoKwik, Shopflo, Razorpay, Shiprocket and Cashfree Payments. These domestic rivals offer specialised, India-centric capabilities like returns management, shopper engagement and advertising. These may turn out to be a tough nut to crack for Shopify. The Ultimate Test: Shop Pay’s success in India will eventually depend on whether its native integration platform can outperform local checkout rivals on pricing, conversion and localised features. To win, Shopify must prove that Shop Pay can deliver higher net margins and lower overall operational costs than entrenched domestic alternatives. As Shopify gears up to launch Shop Pay in India, can the SaaS giant turn its brand equity and distribution advantage into a meaningful Indian checkout business? Let’s find out… RECOMMENDED FOR yOU From The Editor’s Desk 🏭 Zetwerk IPO Day 1 The B2B manufacturing startup’s public issue was subscribed just 23% on the first day of bidding, receiving bids for 4.
paragraph2: 17 Cr shares against 18.51 Cr shares on offer. The public offer saw the highest interest from QIBs, followed by retail investors and NIIs. Zetwerk’s ₹5,000 Cr IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹2,830 Cr and an OFS component of up to 14.45 Cr shares. At the upper end of its ₹143-₹151 IPO price band, the issue values the company at around ₹25,583 Cr. Separately, Tonbo Imaging’s IPO was oversubscribed 4X at the end of the first day, receiving bidding for 3.4 Cr shares against 85.3 Lakh shares on offer. The defence tech startup’s issue consists entirely of an OFS of up to 1.2 Cr shares worth ₹852 Cr. 📉 JFS’ Profit Halves In Q2 Jio Financial Services’ consolidated net profit declined 51% YoY to ₹340.4 Cr in Q2 FY27. This came despite operating revenue zooming 73% to ₹1,699.3 Cr in the quarter under review. The company attributed the decline in profits to higher expenditure and the absence of dividend income during the quarter.
paragraph3: Total expenses jumped 167% YoY to ₹1,166.1 Cr in the quarter ended September 2026. On the operational front, JFS’ NBFC arm, Jio Credit, had ₹37,320 Cr in AUM at the end of September 2026, while its digital payments vertical clocked a total payment value of ₹14,682 Cr in the quarter. title_bn: Goldman Sachs Sells Eternal Shares Via A ₹169 Cr Block Deal
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Financial service giant Goldman Sachs has sold 53.4 Lakh shares of foodtech giant Eternal in a major block deal worth…
paragraph1: SUMMARYAccording to NSE data, the investment bank, via its entity Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, sold the shares at ₹316 apiece to rake in the amount The block deal comes as the investor looks to book profits amid a sharp uptick in Eternal’s share prices in recent months and improving financials The shares that flooded the market were lapped up by Bank of America, via its affiliate BofA Securities Europe, for ₹168.7 Cr Financial service giant Goldman Sachs has sold 53.4 Lakh shares of foodtech giant Eternal in a major block deal worth ₹168.7 Cr. According to NSE data, the investment bank, via its entity Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, sold the shares at ₹316 apiece to rake in the amount.
paragraph2: The investor offloaded the stake at a discount of more than 2.6% to the stock’s last closing price on Thursday. The shares that flooded the market were lapped up by Bank of America, via its affiliate BofA Securities Europe, for ₹168.7 Cr. This is the second block witnessed by Eternal in the past two months.
paragraph3: In early September, French financial services giant BNP Paribas and US-based hedge fund Millennium Management together sold over 9.9 Cr shares of the listed foodtech giant for a sum of ₹3,264.8 Cr. This latest block deal comes as investors continue to be bullish on Eternal. Shares of the foodtech giant have surged nearly 10% in the past three months, and are up 16.
paragraph4: 2% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. The uptick in Eternal’s shares has come on the back of strong financial performance by the startup despite intensifying competition in the quick commerce space and the entry of new players like Rapido’s Ownly, Flipkart and Swish. What has been powering the stock’s rise is Eternal’s quick commerce arm Blinkit, which continues to dominate the instant delivery market. On the financial front, Eternal reported a consolidated net profit of ₹92 Cr in Q1 FY27, up nearly 3.7X from ₹25 Cr in the year-ago quarter.
paragraph5: Meanwhile, operating revenue surged 182% YoY and 17% QoQ to ₹20,211 Cr during the quarter under review. Shares of Eternal closed Thursday’s trading session 2.77% higher at ₹324.35 on the BSE.

title: Inside SEBI’s 10 Key Proposed Changes To SME IPO Rules
title_bn: Inside SEBI’s 10 Key Proposed Changes To SME IPO Rules
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed sweeping changes to the rules governing initial public offerings (IPOs)…
paragraph1: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed sweeping changes to the rules governing initial public offerings (IPOs) of small and medium enterprises (SMEs). In a consultation paper floated on October 14, the markets regulator has proposed changes to SME IPO norms, including regulations pertaining to valuation thresholds, profitability and shareholder exits. The regulator has invited public feedback on the paper till November 4. Citing its rationale, the regulator said that the paper has been formulated by its working group due to rapid increase in the funds raised through SME IPOs and the number of investors participating in such issues. Since launch in 2012, about 1,500 companies have opted to list on the SME platform and have raised ₹40,222 Cr. Startups like Zappfresh, DroneAcharya, TAC Infosec, Yudiz, are a few startups that have also taken this route to go public. In view of this, the regulator has proposed multiple changes, including lowering the minimum application threshold and removing mandatory underwriting and market-making requirements. Here’s a look at some of the key changes that have been proposed: The Market Cap-Based Listing Criteria Under the proposed framework, companies with a post-issue market capitalisation of ₹1,000 Cr or less can now list on the SME platform. Those valued in the range of ₹1,000 Cr to ₹4,000 Cr can also choose to list either on the SME platform or the main board. Companies valued over ₹4,000 Cr will have to list on the main board. SEBI has also proposed replacing the existing paid-up share capital criterion with post-issue market capitalisation to determine whether a company can list on the SME platform or the main board. Currently, companies with post-issue paid-up share capital of up to ₹25 Cr can opt for the SME platform, subject to other eligibility conditions.
paragraph2: In addition, companies in the ₹1,000 Cr to ₹4,000 Cr band choosing the SME platform would also have to submit restated consolidated financial statements under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) for the preceding three financial years, if they have not already adopted Ind AS. If an IPO applicant’s estimated market capitalisation crosses the applicable threshold during the IPO process, it would have to refile under the relevant listing framework. Minimum Profitability Requirements Raised SEBI has proposed mandating SME IPO applicants to report an average operating profit of at least ₹3 Cr annually over the preceding three financial years, based on restated consolidated financial statements. In contrast, the existing framework requires operating profit of at least ₹1 Cr in at least two of the preceding three fiscal years. However, the consultation paper refers to EBIT in its narrative, while existing provision mentioned EBITDA. This requires clarification. Companies that fail the proposed profitability test could still list on the SME platform through an alternative route. They would have to use the book-building process and allocate at least 75% of the net offer to qualified institutional buyers (QIBs). If the required allocation is not achieved, the entire subscription amount would have to be refunded. New Rules For Converted And Reorganised Businesses SEBI has proposed changing the eligibility rules for SMEs seeking an IPO after converting from a proprietorship, partnership or limited liability partnership (LLP). These draft rules also cover companies undergoing qualifying business reorganisations. Currently, such companies generally need to complete at least one full financial year before filing their draft IPO papers.
paragraph3: Under the new proposal, they would need to complete four consecutive financial quarters from the date of conversion or qualifying reorganisation and submit at least one annual audited financial statement prepared after the change. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU The proposal also covers acquisitions, succession and schemes of arrangement, where more than 50% of the revenue comes from businesses that previously operated as proprietorships, partnerships or LLPs. In such cases, the earlier business’ operating track record could be considered when assessing IPO eligibility. The ₹10 Cr Cap On GCP Allocation May Go SEBI has proposed removing the ₹10 Cr cap on the amount that the companies can allocate, from their IPO proceeds, towards general corporate purposes (GCP). Currently, GCP allocation cannot exceed 15% of the amount raised or ₹10 Cr, whichever is lower. Under the proposal, the 15% limit would remain, but the fixed ₹10 Cr ceiling would be removed, allowing companies raising larger amounts to allocate more funds to general business needs. SEBI Looks To Reshuffle OFS Rules SEBI has also proposed a dedicated offer-for-sale (OFS) framework with a one-year holding requirement, subject to specified exemptions. The draft framework also seeks to remove the existing 20% ceiling on the OFS component for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs). The Primary Market Advisory Committee (PMAC) went a step further and suggested removing the 50% cap on a QIB’s pre-issue holding as well. These exemptions, however, would not apply to companies using the alternative listing route after failing the proposed profitability test. Lock-In Periods To Be Revised SEBI has proposed revising the lock-in periods for promoters and other shareholders after an SME IPO. The draft changes include: Minimum promoters’ contribution: The three-year lock-in on minimum promoter contribution would begin from the IPO allotment date.
paragraph4: In contrast, the lock-in date is currently linked to the commencement of commercial production. Promoter holdings above the minimum contribution: The existing staggered lock-in would be replaced with a uniform one-year lock-in. Non-promoter pre-issue capital: The lock-in will reduce from the current one year to six months. Promoter group holdings: A separate one-year lock-in would apply from the IPO allotment date. Depositories could also mark shares that cannot be locked in electronically as non-transferable for the applicable period. SEBI to Further Trim Minimum IPO Application Threshold The markets regulator has proposed lowering the minimum application amount for SME IPOs to ₹1 Lakh from the existing requirement of more than ₹2 Lakh. Investors would have to apply for at least four lots worth a minimum of ₹25,000 each. The ₹2 Lakh minimum was introduced in March 2025 to limit participation by smaller retail investors. The consultation paper also proposes aligning investor categories and allocation rules more closely with the mainboard framework, including the introduction of the ‘Retail Individual Investor’ category. Under the regime, Issuers can also allocate up to 60% of the QIB portion to anchor investors in book-built issues. SEBI has also proposed increasing the minimum number of allottees from 200 to 500. Under the alternative route for companies failing the profitability test, up to 10% of the net offer would go to retail investors, up to 15% to NIIs and at least 75% to QIBs.
paragraph5: SME Shares Could Be Traded In Lots Of One SEBI has proposed allowing investors to trade SME-listed shares in lots of one share, replacing the existing price-linked lot sizes. The consultation paper notes that around 5% of unique PAN-based shareholders held odd-lot shares, on average. The proposed change could make it easier for investors to sell their entire holdings, but it will not change the minimum IPO application amount. End For Mandatory Underwriting And Market-Making? SEBI has proposed removing mandatory underwriting and market-making requirements for SME IPOs to reduce listing costs. Currently, SME IPOs must be fully underwritten, with lead managers required to underwrite at least 15% of the issue themselves. Under the proposal, these requirements would be removed. The 75% QIB portion under the alternative listing route would not need to be underwritten. Underwriting fees accounted for 49.52% and 38.
