title: Flipkart Group FY26: Revenue Nears ₹1.5 Lakh Cr, Loss Narrows To ₹8,468 Cr
title_bn: Flipkart Group FY26: Revenue Nears ₹1.5 Lakh Cr, Loss Narrows To ₹8,468 Cr
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Flipkart Group reported an 18.2% jump in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in the fiscal year 2025-26…
paragraph1: SUMMARYFlipkart Group reported an 18% YoY jump in consolidated operating revenue to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in FY26, while net loss narrowed marginally by 2.1% YoY to ₹8,468 Cr The numbers reflect the performance of the Flipkart Group as a whole. This comes as the ecommerce giant completed its reverse flip from Singapore to India in March 2026 On the operational front, the company said that its gross margins rose 23% YoY in FY26, while adjusted EBITDA improved by around ₹1,500 Cr during the fiscal Flipkart Group reported an 18.2% jump in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in the fiscal year 2025-26 (FY26), up from ₹1.23 Lakh Cr in the year ago fiscal. Meanwhile, its consolidated net loss narrowed marginally by 2.1% to ₹8,468 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹8,646 Cr in FY25.
paragraph2: The numbers reflect the performance of the Flipkart Group as a whole, rather than the standalone financials of the Flipkart ecommerce marketplace. The financial results come after the Walmart-backed ecommerce giant completed its reverse flip from Singapore to India in March 2026. The restructuring brought the group’s holding structure back to India, ahead of a potential domestic public listing. The consolidated entity includes businesses such as Myntra and Cleartrip, alongside logistics, platform services and other specialised operations. “As part of its re-domiciliation to India, (the) Flipkart Group is publishing consolidated financial results under Flipkart Internet Private Limited. The results reflect the group’s performance over the reporting period for the year ended March 2026 and provide a historical view of the business rather than a current trading update,” said the ecommerce giant in a blog post. On the operational front, the company said that its gross margins rose 23% YoY in FY26, while adjusted EBITDA improved by around ₹1,500 Cr during the fiscal. “Adjusted operating margin improved by 230 basis points, from -7.7% to -5.
paragraph3: 4%, supported by higher gross margins and lower overheads,” added the ecommerce major. Flipkart also noted its adjusted operating business losses, before finance costs, tax, other income and exceptional items, narrowed by 17%, or around ₹1,600 Cr, during the fiscal under review. However, this improvement in operating losses translated into only a marginal reduction in net losses. Flipkart attributed the higher net losses to higher finance costs, the derecognition of deferred tax assets recognised in earlier periods and certain exceptional items. How Did Flipkart’s B2C Arm Perform? Meanwhile, the ecommerce major’s B2C arm, Flipkart Internet Private Limited, reported a 19.3% YoY decline in revenue from operations to ₹16,295 Cr in FY26 compared with ₹20,202 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. Including other income of ₹744 Cr (down from ₹947 Cr in FY25), the B2C vertical’s total income stood at ₹17,039 Cr in FY26, 19.4% lower than ₹21,149 Cr in the previous fiscal.
paragraph4: On the expenses front, Flipkart Internet Pvt Ltd’s total expenses fell 3.6% to ₹22,522 Cr from ₹23,361 Cr in FY25. Overall, the B2C business’ net loss rose to ₹5,498 Cr in FY26 from ₹1,694 Cr a year earlier. Notably, the FY25 figures were restated to account for the business combination. Where Did Flipkart Group Spend In FY26? Despite the growing top line and narrowing losses, Flipkart Group’s total expenses rose 16% to ₹1.54 Lakh Cr in FY26 as against ₹1.33 Lakh Cr in the year-ago period. Purchase Of Traded Goods: This was the biggest cost-centre for the company.
paragraph5: Expenses under this head climbed 17.4% YoY to ₹1.17 Lakh Cr in the fiscal under review. Employee Benefit Expenses: The group’s employee benefit costs remained relatively flat at ₹8,376 Cr compared with ₹8,268 Cr in FY25. Finance Costs: Expenditure under this bucket nearly doubled to ₹1,209 Cr from ₹649 Cr in FY25. Logistics & Storage Service Charges: Expenses under this header stood at ₹15,154 Cr in FY26, up 28.9% from ₹11,759 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. The expense accounted for nearly 54% of the group’s total other expenses of ₹28,277 Cr in FY26, highlighting the cost of running its logistics, warehousing and delivery operations.

title: Why CoreWeaves troubles are rattling the AI boom
title_bn: Why CoreWeaves troubles are rattling the AI boom
author: TechPulse
excerpt: COREWEAVE-STOCKS/ (EXPLAINER, PIX):EXPLAINER-Why CoreWeave's troubles are rattling the AI boom
paragraph1: By Anhata Rooprai and Aditya SoniOct 15 (Reuters) - CoreWeave's mounting debt is raising fresh concerns about the AI boom, as investors question whether demand can justify the billions being borrowed to build data centres.Shares and bonds of the Nvidia-backed company have tumbleddespite its CEO's assurances of a strong contract backlog, fueling a broader selloff in technology stocks.Here is why investors are worried and what its troubles could mean for the industry.WHAT DOES COREWEAVE DO?CoreWeave rents out computing power from Nvidia processors to companies developing and running AI, including Microsoft and OpenAI.It is one of the leading "neocloud" providers, a group of newer cloud companies that are growing rapidly to meet demand for scarce and expensive AI chips.These neocloud companies give customers access to computing power without requiring them to build their own data centers. However, supplying such capacity requires heavy upfront investment in chips and infrastructure, often financed with debt.WHAT IS ITS FINANCIAL SITUATION?
paragraph2: The company, which has never turned a profit, has about $50 billion in debt, according to data compiled by LSEG.It raised its annual capital spending forecast by $4 billion in August to between $35 billion and $39 billion. Analysts expect revenue of nearly $13 billion this year and a loss of $2.13 billion.The yields on its bonds due in 2031, which are rated junk, have spiked to about 16%, while the cost of insuring its debt against default has climbed to about 1,000 basis points, reflecting growing concern among creditors.CEO Mike Intrator told employees in an internal memo seen by Reuters that its deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations. The company had a $104.2 billion revenue backlog at the end of the second quarter, followed by more than $25 billion in new commitments early in the third quarter.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has also downplayed the concerns, saying CoreWeave's financial strength is improving and he sees no need to backstop it.
paragraph3: The chip giant has agreed to buy unsold CoreWeave capacity through April 2032.WHY IT COULD BE A CANARY IN THE COAL MINECoreWeave's business depends on two things: demand for AI computing and lenders' willingness to finance the infrastructure supplying it. But a selloff in its shares suggests a lack of confidence among investors in the latter, even as the company cites strong demand.The concern is not that AI demand will collapse, but that higher borrowing costs could make the business harder to sustain if demand were to weaken sharply."It looks more like investors questioning how the build-out is being funded than a sudden collapse in appetite for AI computing," said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG Group."CoreWeave is quickly becoming the AI trade's canary in the coal mine," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB.WHY ARE MARKETS FRETTING?Investors are questioning whether AI revenue can grow fast enough to cover the cost of building and financing the infrastructure.CoreWeave has to spend heavily upfront before it can collect the revenue from its contracts.
paragraph4: Higher interest rates could drive up financing costs and further squeeze returns.The hardware itself poses another risk. Chips lose value as newer generations arrive, pushing providers to spend even more to replace them.The concerns, however, go beyond CoreWeave. US technology giants are expected to spend more than $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year.THE DOWNSIDE SCENARIOOne potential consequence would be a broader financing squeeze, with lenders demanding higher returns or becoming less willing to fund other AI projects.That could force providers to scale back expansion, curbing equipment purchases and affecting the computing capacity customers expect.A setback could also deepen doubts that the AI investment frenzy is outpacing returns, piling further pressure on technology stocks.The impact of the fallout would depend on how the business is reorganized, and CoreWeave's ties to major technology companies do not, by themselves, mean its failure would trigger a wider financial crisis.
paragraph5: WHO ELSE BEARS THE RISK?Gartner estimates about 80% of neoclouds could shut down by 2030, warning that expected AI revenue will not support profitable returns on all planned infrastructure spending.Neocloud rivals Nebius, Applied Digital and Iren have fallen in the recent selloff. The cost of default protection has risen for SoftBank, which is betting heavily on OpenAI.Meanwhile, spreads for Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Nvidia have also reached records, although they have risen much more slowly than CoreWeave's. However, these companies also have larger cash flows and stronger balance sheets.

title: Origin Bags $20 Mn To Build Autonomous Construction Robots
title_bn: Origin Bags $20 Mn To Build Autonomous Construction Robots
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Emerging out of stealth mode, robotics startup Origin has raised $20 Mn (around ₹189 Cr) in a funding round co-led…
paragraph1: SUMMARYThe startup said that the fresh capital will primarily be utilised to deploy a fleet of 150 construction robots by 2027-end and support new pilots in the US and Europe Founded in 2025, Origin develops autonomous robotics for construction work. Its flagship model OG-1 can perform tasks such as sanding and priming As part of the investment, Zacua Ventures’ founding partner Vivin Hegde has also joined the startup’s board as a director Emerging out of stealth mode, robotics startup Origin has raised $20 Mn (around ₹189 Cr) in a funding round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures. The round also saw participation from Unilazer Ventures, Schema Ventures and Z21. Angel investors from Anduril, Skild AI, 1X and Tesla also participated in the fundraise.
paragraph2: As part of the investment, Zacua Ventures’ founding partner Vivin Hegde has also joined the startup’s board as a director. The startup said that the fresh capital will primarily be utilised to deploy its flagship OG-1 robot and build a fleet of construction robots. A chunk of the capital will also be used to support “large-scale” pilots with customers in the US and Europe and explore new use cases for bots. “We think of Origin as a time machine for construction, helping crews complete work faster while moving the industry toward autonomous job sites.
paragraph3: Wall finishing and painting are only our starting trades; our ambition is to automate the full range of interior trades so contractors can build faster with consistent quality,” said Origin cofounder and CEO Yogesh Ghaturle. Founded in 2025 by Ghaturle, Ashish Daga and Tushar Makkar, the US-headquartered startup develops autonomous robotics for construction work. It aims to address widespread labour shortages in the construction sector and claims that its robots can work 3X faster than a human. Its flagship robot, OG-1, is currently capable of automatically completing wall-finishing tasks such as applying compound, sanding, and priming.
paragraph4: The startup claims to have already deployed its robots at construction sites in New York, adding that its bots are also being deployed across commercial spaces, apartments, data centers, hotels and warehouses. Under the hood, OG-1 is powered by a proprietary foundation model that the startup calls a construction action model. The model integrates a reasoning system to plan complex sub-tasks, an action policy to help it navigate autonomously and a controller for feedback-driven movement. Going forward, the startup plans to deploy 150 robots by the end of 2027.
paragraph5: It is also exploring additional pilots for its offerings in countries like Germany, Sweden, France and Saudi Arabia. Origin also noted that incoming investor Zacua will support its expansion plans through its network of contractors, developers and manufacturers. With the latest fundraise, Origin is eyeing a piece of the global construction robotics sector, which is projected to become a $12 Bn opportunity by 2036. Back home in India, startups like Pace Robotics and Flo Mobility are also raising big bucks to take a lead in the burgeoning space.

title: [Update] Zetwerk IPO Subscribed 23% On Day 1
title_bn: [Update] Zetwerk IPO Subscribed 23% On Day 1
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Update | October 10, 19:03 B2B manufacturing company Zetwerk’s IPO received muted response on day one as it was subscribed…
paragraph1: SUMMARYZetwerk’s ₹5,012.3 Cr IPO was subscribed 8% with investors bidding for 1.5 Lakh shares against 18.5 Cr shares on offer Employees subscribed to 19% of their allocation while retail individual investors bid for 15% of the shares reserved for them The IPO values the B2B manufacturing startup at around ₹25,583 Cr at the upper end of the price band Update | October 10, 19:03 B2B manufacturing company Zetwerk’s IPO received muted response on day one as it was subscribed just 23%. The issue received bids for 4.17 Cr shares against 18.51 Cr shares on offer. The offer saw the highest subscription from qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) who placed 2.96 Cr shares against their quota of 9.89 Cr shares, or 30% subscription.
paragraph2: Retail individual investors bid for 74.32 Lakh shares out of the 3.42 Cr shares reserved for them, translating to a 22% subscription of their quota. Non-institutional investors (NIIs) placed bids for 44.08 Lakh shares, or just 9% of their quota of 5.13 Cr shares. Meanwhile, Zetwerk’s employees placed bids for 1.84 Lakh shares or subscribed to 26% of the 7 Lakh shares earmarked for them. Original | October 10, 14:24 B2B manufacturing company Zetwerk’s ₹5,012.3 Cr IPO got off to a rather slow start today, receiving a mere 8% subscription as of 14:00 IST.
paragraph3: Investors have placed bids for 1.50 Cr shares against 18.51 Cr shares on offer, as per BSE data. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) have been the most bullish on the public float till now, placing the highest number of bids for 75.67 Lakh shares. However, this translated to a mere 8% subscription of their quota of 9.89 Cr shares. Retail individual investors followed closely as they bid for 51.79 Lakh against 3.42 Cr shares reserved for them, translating to a 15% subscription of their quota.
paragraph4: Non-institutional investors (NIIs) subscribed to just 4% of their earmarked portion, bidding for 21.55 Lakh out of 5.13 Cr shares allocated to them. Meanwhile, employees of the manufacturing company placed bids for 1.34 Lakh shares against the 7 Lakh shares reserved for them, subscribing to their quota by 19%. Zetwerk’s IPO closes on October 19. The company set a price band of ₹143-₹151 per share for its IPO, indicating a valuation of around ₹25,583 Cr at the upper end. The issue comprises a fresh issue of ₹2,830 Cr and an offer for share component of up to 14.45 Cr shares, worth ₹2,182.3 Cr at the upper end, as per its RHP.
paragraph5: Ahead of opening the issue, Zetwerk raised ₹2,251.2 Cr from anchor investors yesterday. Domestic mutual funds including SBI Mutual Fund and ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund accounted for around 46% of the anchor book, while global institutional investors like Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and ADIA also picked up stake. Founded in 2018 by Amrit Acharya, Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Vishal Chaudhary, Zetwerk operates a full-stack manufacturing platform serving businesses across industrial and consumer goods categories. It combines capacity from third-party suppliers and its own facilities to manage manufacturing orders across sectors including renewable energy, consumer electronics, aerospace, defence, oil and gas, and industrial automation. The company has raised over $900 Mn in funding to date from investors like Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Accel India, Greenoaks Capital Partners, and D1 Capital Partners. On the financial front, Zetwerk posted a consolidated net loss of ₹733 Cr in Q1 FY27 against operating revenue of ₹4,117.9 Cr.

title: Rabot Energy secures $50M to transform homes into a virtual power plant
title_bn: Rabot Energy secures $50M to transform homes into a virtual power plant
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Rabot Energy, a provider of dynamic electricity tariffs,has raised $50 million in a Series B funding round to expand its technologyplatform and support its next phase of growth. The round was led by E...
paragraph1: Rabot Energy, a provider of dynamic electricity tariffs, has raised $50 million in a Series B funding round to expand its technology platform and support its next phase of growth. The round was led by Endeit, a growth capital investor focused on European tech scale-ups, alongside the DeepTech & Climate Fonds (DTCF). Existing investors HV Capital, High-Tech Gründerfonds (HTGF), Bosch Ventures, CNI, Acurio Ventures and vent.io also participated.
paragraph2: Rabot Energy offers dynamic electricity tariffs that help customers reduce energy costs by automatically shifting electricity consumption to periods when power is cheaper, and renewable energy is more readily available. Its technology also enables connected home batteries to store electricity when renewable generation is high and release it when supply is lower, helping balance demand and reduce reliance on fossil fuel-based generation. As transport and heating become increasingly electrified and renewable energy generation expands, the company aims to make electricity consumption more flexible by connecting household energy devices and managing their consumption and storage. In June 2026, Rabot Energy launched Rabot Flow, combining a dynamic electricity tariff, a smart meter and a plug-and-play home battery.
paragraph3: According to the company, the solution can reduce household energy costs by 15 per cent. The battery connects to a standard socket, requires no rooftop solar installation and can also be used by renters. Rabot Energy is also developing a virtual power plant (VPP) model that aggregates connected home batteries, allowing electricity storage and consumption to be coordinated across households to support grid flexibility. The next generation of power plants will not be built; it will be connected.
paragraph4: Millions of households have enormous untapped potential to do more than simply consume energy and instead become an active part of the wider energy system, said Jan Rabe, CEO of Rabot Energy. Over the past three and a half years, Rabot Energy has grown to more than 200,000 customers, including around 15,000 commercial and industrial clients, and reached €200 million in revenue. With the new funding, Rabot Energy aims to reach one million customers, expand its offering for residential, commercial and industrial customers across Germany, and further develop its proprietary technology platform. The company also plans to connect additional energy devices, including home batteries, electric vehicle chargers and heat pumps, to increase flexibility across its network.

title: AI: Europe’s 10 most-funded companies in H1 2026
title_bn: AI: Europe’s 10 most-funded companies in H1 2026
author: TechPulse
excerpt: European AI funding in H1 2026 was characterised by a highconcentration of capital in a few large transactions, alongside abroad base of smaller investments. Several rounds exceeded €500 million,highl...
paragraph1: European AI funding in H1 2026 was characterised by a high concentration of capital in a few large transactions, alongside a broad base of smaller investments. Several rounds exceeded €500 million, highlighting the capital-intensive nature of advanced AI research and infrastructure development. At the same time, numerous seed and pre-seed rounds reflected continued investment in early-stage AI companies. Geographically, the UK led in both funding value and deal activity, followed by France and Germany. Together, these three markets attracted the vast majority of capital, while smaller investments across the Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland, the Nordics and Central and Eastern Europe reflected the broader geographical spread of Europe's AI ecosystem. The industry also showed increasing diversification, with funding supporting AI models, computing hardware and data infrastructure, alongside applications in healthcare, manufacturing, financial services and cybersecurity. For further insights into funding trends across the European technology ecosystem, check out Tech.eu's Funding Explorer, free and open to everyone.
paragraph2: Here are the companies that raised the most in H1 2026. 1 Ineffable Intelligence (UK) Amount raised in H1 2026: $1.1B Ineffable Intelligence is a UK-based AI research company working to develop systems capable of learning autonomously. Its approach centres on reinforcement learning, aiming to create a “superlearner” that can continuously acquire new knowledge and skills through experience rather than relying on human-generated data. The company is exploring an alternative path towards advanced artificial intelligence, with a focus on systems that can discover knowledge independently. In H1 2026, Ineffable Intelligence raised $1.1 billion to support the development of its autonomous learning technology and advance its research into superintelligence. 2 Advanced Machine Intelligence (France) Amount raised in H1 2026: $1B Paris-based Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI Labs) is developing AI systems designed to understand and predict how the physical world works.
paragraph3: The company focuses on world models as an alternative to traditional large language models. Rather than relying primarily on text-based predictions, its technology aims to enable machines to reason about real-world environments, anticipate outcomes and develop a deeper understanding of physical reality. AMI Labs secured $1 billion in H1 2026 to advance its world model research and build teams across Paris, New York, Montreal and Singapore. 3 Mistral AI (France) Amount raised in H1 2026: $830M Mistral AI is a French artificial intelligence company developing large language models and generative AI solutions for businesses, developers and public institutions. Positioned as a European alternative to major US AI providers, the company focuses on open-weight models, customisable AI systems and infrastructure that gives organisations greater control over their data and technology. Its strategy includes expanding European computing capacity to support AI model training and deployment while reducing reliance on external cloud providers. During H1 2026, Mistral AI secured $830 million in debt financing to purchase 13,800 Nvidia GPUs for its first data centre in France, supporting the expansion of its AI infrastructure. 4 Recursive Superintelligence (UK) Amount raised in H1 2026: $650M Recursive Superintelligence is a London-based AI startup developing systems capable of improving their own intelligence without continuous human intervention.
paragraph4: The company is exploring recursive self-improvement as a path towards advanced artificial intelligence. Its initial focus is on developing AI that can improve other AI systems through automated research, with longer-term ambitions to apply these methods across scientific disciplines. In H1 2026, Recursive Superintelligence raised $650 million to advance its research into self-improving AI systems and develop technology for automated scientific discovery. 5 ElevenLabs (UK) Amount raised in H1 2026: $561M London-headquartered ElevenLabs was founded in 2022 and specialises in AI-generated voice and audio technology. Its platform enables users to generate realistic speech, clone voices, dub content into multiple languages and create sound effects. Originally focused on text-to-speech technology, the company has expanded into conversational AI, offering voice agents for customer support, sales, marketing and internal business operations. Its technology is used by businesses, developers and content creators worldwide. ElevenLabs raised approximately $561 million across funding transactions in H1 2026 to expand its enterprise AI agents, advance research into conversational models and audio technology, and support international growth.
paragraph5: 6 Parloa (Germany) Amount raised in H1 2026: $350M Berlin-based Parloa develops conversational AI technology that enables businesses to automate customer interactions across voice, chat and messaging channels. The company provides an AI agent management platform that combines speech recognition and natural language understanding to handle customer enquiries and support tasks. Its technology is used by companies including Allianz, Booking.com and SAP, helping customer service teams manage interactions at scale while reducing reliance on traditional call centre processes.

title: Nebius says struck deals with UK AI labs, welcomes non-compete changes
title_bn: Nebius says struck deals with UK AI labs, welcomes non-compete changes
author: TechPulse
excerpt: European AI infrastructure company Nebius says it has struck deals with a number of early-stage UK AI labs as it looks to accelerate its compute and infrastructure offering in the UK.Nebius, which is ...
paragraph1: European AI infrastructure company Nebius says it has struck deals with a number of early-stage UK AI labs as it looks to accelerate its compute and infrastructure offering in the UK. Nebius, which is sometimes referred to as a neocloud, builds and operates data centres, packing them with GPUs, then offers access to these data centres to AI and enterprise companies needing compute power, as well as offering them specialised software to run AI applications. Earlier this year, Nebius announced a £1.7bn UK build-out across new sites, along wtth an expansion of its London hub, which is its major European R&D and go-to-market hub.
paragraph2: Nebius, which is headquartered in Amsterdam and has bagged multi-billion-dollar contracts with Meta and Microsoft to supply them with AI infrastructure, has four data centre sites in the UK. Nebius, which has also struck compute deals with Revolut and Prima Mente, also has its own data centres in Finland and France. Nebius general manager, EMEA, Gary Tierney, said Nebius wanted to “continue to look to expand” in the UK, referencing its talent density. He said: “We are working with some really exciting AI labs that are coming out of the UK.
paragraph3: ” Tierney did not provide specific details on which UK AI labs it was working with but said they were in stealth or just came out of stealth. London-based AI lab Ineffable Intelligence, founded by former DeepMind bigwig David Silver; Inherent, founded by former DeepMind, Microsoft and White House staff; and Recursive Superintelligence, co-founded by high-profile German computer scientist Richard Socher, are examples of UK AI startups coming out of stealth this year. Ineffable Intelligence has struck a deal with Google Cloud to be its preferred cloud partner. Asked more broadly about the public backlash against data centres in the UK, Tierney said: “I don’t think that is ever a reason for us not to invest in a region” pointing to its investment in the UK.
paragraph4: Separately, Tierney said he was pleased the UK government was planning to ease restrictive non-compete clauses in workers' employment contracts. He added: “It’s not necessarily been a problem for us. But we service the startup market. And when you look at that non-compete not existing in the US, you see the startup market is moving way quicker.
paragraph5: “Here, now with so much great talent appearing and being able to raise funds but they can’t attract talent in London, because of this non-compete, if that goes away, I think you are going to see an emergence of a lot more labs, a lot more frontier builders here in the UK."

WhatsApp has introduced Guest Calling.WhatsApp has introduced its Guest Calling feature, allowing people without a WhatsApp account to join voice and video calls through a shared link.Launched by WhatsApp, owned by Meta, on 15th October 2026, the new addition aims to make online meetings, group discussions, tutoring sessions, and personal chats more convenient. Users may sign in via their computer browser without making an account or downloading the WhatsApp application.The new feature lets WhatsApp users invite others outside the app while still ensuring that only those they choose are part of a WhatsApp conversation. Guest calls are free, end-to-end encrypted and have no time limits, according to WhatsApp's official announcement.Up to 32 people are allowed for group calls.
paragraph2: The company has also revealed that it will offer Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook integration later this year, making call scheduling easier.WhatsApp Guest Calling: How does it work?Guest Calling lets an existing WhatsApp user generate a call link and share it with other people. The link can be opened in a web browser on the recipient's computer, with the required entry information being the name and a request for access to the call. They don't have to register on WhatsApp or download the app to join.However, only WhatsApp account holders can create call links. All guests must remain in a virtual waiting room until the host grants access to their requests. The host may also terminate a participant at any time, without losing control of the conversation.WhatsApp says guests can use several calling features, including computer screen sharing, thumbs-up and heart emoji reactions, and the option to raise their hands to indicate that they want to speak.
paragraph3: How to join a WhatsApp call without an accountTo be a part of a voice or video call as a guest user, follow these steps:Receive a call link: Ask a WhatsApp user to create one and share it with you.Open the link: Use a web browser on your computer to click on the invitation link.Your name: Provide your name when prompted to identify yourself to the host.Request access: Submit your request to join the call.Wait for permission: You will remain in the waiting room until the host admits you.Join the conversation: After logging in, join the voice or video call and take advantage of the in-call features.There's no need for guests to register for a new account or download WhatsApp to use this feature. To create the invitation, the host needs to have a WhatsApp account.What can guests do during WhatsApp calls?
paragraph4: There are a few restrictions with guest access. Participants cannot see other participants' cell phone numbers, send messages, or directly invite more people to the call. The host controls who joins and stays in the conversation.The feature can be used for one-to-one calls or group calls with up to 32 participants. Guest calling is end-to-end encrypted, which can help protect conversations, WhatsApp adds.WhatsApp to add Google Calendar and Outlook integrationLater in 2026, WhatsApp will also be adding integrations with Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook. Users can generate WhatsApp call links directly in their calendars and add them as event invitations, the company says.The integration requires users to install the WhatsApp plugin and link their account. Invitees can join the calls scheduled via the shared link, even if they don't have a WhatsApp account.

title: Incoming calls to show caller names from November 1: What mobile users need to know
title_bn: Incoming calls to show caller names from November 1: What mobile users need to know
author: TechPulse
excerpt: India will roll out mandatory Calling Name Presentation (CNAP) from November 1, 2026, displaying callers' names alongside phone numbers on 4G and 5G networks. Here's how the new caller ID system will work, its privacy safeguards and rules for busines
paragraph1: India will roll out mandatory Calling Name Presentation (CNAP) from November 1, 2026, displaying callers' names alongside phone numbers on 4G and 5G networks. Here's how the new caller ID system will work, its privacy safeguards and rules for businesses using registered names.Unknown callers to show their names from November 1.(AI generated image for representational purposes only)The Government of India will make caller name identification mandatory for mobile users from November 1, 2026, to help people identify incoming calls from unknown numbers. The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has urged telecom service providers to enable Calling Name Presentation (CNAP), which will show the caller's name along with the phone number by default on 4G and new technologies such as 5G networks.The new system is designed to enhance caller identification and assist users in identifying legitimate calls from potentially fraudulent calls. The DoT order has made it necessary for telecom operators to display names using subscriber information stored in their databases. However, the rollout for 2G and 3G networks, as well as landline connections, will be considered separately.
paragraph2: How will the new caller ID system work? When a call arrives, the recipient's phone will show the caller's phone number and name. If the number is saved in the recipient's contacts, the saved name will be displayed, the DoT order said. If the number is not saved, the name the caller entered in the telecom operator's system will appear.For international calls, the screen will show “International Call”. For the system to operate, each telecommunications service provider needs to create and maintain a database that connects subscribers' names to their telephone numbers. The receiving operator will retrieve the necessary data and display it during the incoming call.Will CNAP affect user privacy?
paragraph3: The DoT order has called for the telecom operators to implement a security-by-design methodology. Caller names retrieved through the query-response mechanism cannot be retained after the incoming call ends.Subscribers who have enabled Calling Line Identification Restriction (CLIR) will also be exempt from the system. Their names will not be listed in CNAP.Can businesses display a different caller name?Businesses and bulk connections could be allowed to use a different name from the one found in the operator's subscriber database for display purposes. However, the name must be supported by a registered trademark or a trade name registered on the Goods and Services Tax (GST) portal.It is the operator's responsibility to check the preferred name and supporting documents.
paragraph4: Subscribers who want to update their business name displayed in the results will need to make a request.Why is the government introducing CNAP?The mandate comes after the trials of 4G and 5G networks in recent months. It also incorporates recommendations by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) in February 2024.TRAI agreed to DoT's proposal for making CNAP available by default in October 2025. This was in contrast to its initial proposal, which suggested that the service be turned on only when the user has requested it.The government plans to make caller identification more widely available by leveraging verified subscriber data stored by telecom operators, rather than relying on names saved in phone contacts, with the rollout on November 1, 2026.About the AuthorPragya Singha RoyPragya is a Technology reporter with over four years of experience in digital media and content writing.

title: iPhone Duo inner-screen repair costs $999, more than twice the Galaxy Z Fold 8's cost
title_bn: iPhone Duo inner-screen repair costs $999, more than twice the Galaxy Z Fold 8's cost
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple's iPhone Duo inner display replacement costs $999 in the US, while repairs for other damage can reach $1,499. Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 inner-screen repair costs $419. AppleCare+ cuts the iPhone Duo's accidental-damage repair fee to $99.
paragraph1: Apple's iPhone Duo inner display replacement costs $999 in the US, while repairs for other damage can reach $1,499. Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 inner-screen repair costs $419. AppleCare+ cuts the iPhone Duo's accidental-damage repair fee to $99.Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 vs iPhone Duo(File Photos)Apple has revealed repair costs for its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, ahead of its US launch on October 23, 2026. The company will charge $999 for the inner display, and repairs for certain other types of damage could cost up to $1,499, according to MacRumors.The repair fees are considerable for a device that costs $1,999. Meanwhile, Samsung's estimate for repairing the Galaxy Z Fold 8 in the United States is $419 to replace the inner screen, according to the company’s US repair pricing page. This indicates that the inner display repair price of the iPhone Duo is $580 higher than Samsung, suggesting the cost Apple could face to repair the foldable.
paragraph2: iPhone Duo repair costs without AppleCare+Apple's repair estimates are that the iPhone Duo's inner display is $999 to replace, and damage classified as “other damage” is $1,499. The price of replacing the outer display is $379, while the rear camera and battery replacement fees are $229 each.Apple will sell the repair of the back glass for $199 and the replacement of the removable nano-texture cover layer over the display screen for $49 if the glass is not damaged.Here is the full list of repair charges without AppleCare+:Cover layer: $49Back glass: $199Battery service: $229Rear camera: $229Outer display: $379Work area: $333Inner display: $999Other damage: $1,499Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 repairs cost lessThe Galaxy Z Fold 8 inner-screen replacement is priced at $419 in the US, while the inner-screen replacement on the iPhone Duo costs $999. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra's inner-screen repair costs $479. The Samsung screen module replacement includes additional connected components, and for the Fold 8, it's priced at $579; the Fold 8 Ultra is $ 639.Samsung is also bringing a first-time repair of the Galaxy Z TriFold's inner screen to its refurbished lineup at a promotional price of $699.50.
paragraph3: This is a limited first-repair special but is still $299.50 below the iPhone Duo's inner screen replacement.AppleCare+ reduces iPhone Duo repair chargesAppleCare+ offers a lower-cost option for accidental damage. Coverage for the iPhone Duo costs $19.99 per month, $199.99 annually or $399 upfront.With AppleCare+, inner-display repairs and other accidental-damage repairs cost $99 each. Outer-display and back-glass repairs cost $29, and cover-layer replacement costs $19.
paragraph4: If the battery has less than 80% of the original capacity, the battery service is free. A $149 fee applies to theft or loss claims.The iPhone Duo will go on pre-order on Friday, October 16, and will be released on October 23, 2026. paragraph1: UC Taps Public Markets Again for Funds Urban Company is hungry for more cash. Despite sitting on over hundreds of crores in cash, the consumer services giant’s board will convene next week to consider a fresh fundraise. So, why is Urban Company heading back to the public markets less than a year after its IPO? title: Lawmakers ask FAA to pause use of new AI tool in DC-area flight management
title_bn: Lawmakers ask FAA to pause use of new AI tool in DC-area flight management
author: TechPulse
excerpt: USA-AVIATION:Lawmakers ask FAA to pause use of new AI tool in DC-area flight management
paragraph1: USA-AVIATION:Lawmakers ask FAA to pause use of new AI tool in DC-area flight managementLawmakers ask FAA to pause use of new AI tool in DC-area flight managementBy David ShepardsonWASHINGTON, Oct 13 (Reuters) - More than two dozen lawmakers asked the Federal Aviation Administration to pause the use of a new AI tool in the Washington area to assist air traffic controllers, citing safety concerns.The lawmakers, including Democratic Representatives April Delaney, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Don Beyer, said in a letter they were concerned with the FAA pilot project "as we have not seen any safety evaluation and testing reports, nor have we been made aware of any efforts to train aviation safety personnel on how best to use the tool."The letter seeks an answer by Oct. 19.
paragraph2: "Air traffic control leaves zero margin for error," Ocasio-Cortez said Tuesday, calling for the pause.The FAA last month began using a ​new software-based AI tool ​system that uses predictive ⁠analytics to ​improve how flights ​are managed."We are deeply concerned about the integration of any AI-enabled system into air traffic control systems, where decisions are literally a matter of life or death," said the letter that was also signed by Senator Chris Van Hollen and Representatives Jamie Raskin, Raja Krishnamoorthi and Kweisi Mfume.The FAA in June awarded an $875 million, 12-year contract ​to Air Space Intelligence for a system dubbed Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories or SMART, ‌which uses ⁠data to analyze airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, airspace conditions and operational constraints to predict traffic flows and identify potential conflicts before they occur.
paragraph3: The FAA ⁠is initially using the AI tool in ​the ​airspace ⁠around Washington, D.C. and ​plans to ​gradually ⁠expand it to other parts ⁠of ​the country.Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Tuesday called the tool essentially "dumb AI" and emphasized controllers remain in charge -- not the software.
paragraph4: "Air traffic controllers will always control the airspace. This is just giving additional tools for controllers to better manage" weather and other issues," Duffy said on Fox Business' "Big Money in the Morning."The system uses over 200 data streams, creates data visualizations, and produces scheduling recommendations for operations experts to consider passing along but does not involve active management of planes in the sky, USDOT said."It's going to be transformational," FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told Reuters earlier.
paragraph5: "We'll ​make much better decisions if we have better decision-making tools."The plan is to initially use it to more effectively reschedule ​flights that were canceled due to bad weather with plans to expand to other ​tasks such as strategically coordinating schedules and trajectories before aircraft depart.

title: Nvidias China AI-chip share falls as Huawei closes gap, report finds

author: TechPulse
excerpt: AI-CHINA/CHIPS-NVIDIA (PIX):Nvidia's China AI-chip share fal
paragraph1: * Nvidia's China shipments fell 44% to 678,000 AI chips in the first half* Huawei shipped 572,000 chips, taking 28% of the market to Nvidia's 34%* Trends highlight effect of US export curbs and Beijing's domestic substitution policy* Non-GPU chips surpassed GPUs by volume as Chinese suppliers expanded salesBy Eduardo Baptista and Che PanBEIJING, - Nvidia's share of China's market for data-centre AI chips fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, as US export controls restricted supplies of its products and domestic rivals led by Huawei gained ground, according to an IDC report seen by Reuters.Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators in China from January through June, down 44% from a year earlier, IDC data showed. AI accelerators are specialised chips used to train and run AI models.Washington has restricted China's access to Nvidia's most powerful AI chips, limiting the range of products the US chipmaker can sell in the world's second-largest economy. Beijing, meanwhile, has promoted domestic alternatives and required Chinese companies to seek approval to import compliant Nvidia chips.
paragraph2: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has repeatedly criticised Washington's export curbs, saying the policy forced a US company to cede China's $50 billion AI chip market to Huawei.IDC did not specify which Nvidia products made up its 34% market share, or whether the figure included cutting-edge chips such as the B200 and B300, which are barred from export to China but have been smuggled into the country.Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment.Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators, up from more than 300,000 a year earlier, giving it a 28% share of the overall market, IDC said.Alibaba's chip-design unit T-Head held 7%, followed by Cambricon with 5%, Baidu's Kunlunxin with 4% and Hygon with 3%.
paragraph3: Nine of the 11 Chinese chipmakers tracked by IDC increased shipments from a year earlier.Total AI-accelerator shipments reached 2.008 million units in the first half. Shipments of graphics processing units, or GPUs — the chips most widely used to train AI models — fell 26% to 991,000 units, as supplies eligible for sale in mainland China remained limited, IDC said.Shipments of other AI accelerators rose nearly 80% to 1.
paragraph4: 016 million units, overtaking GPUs by volume. This category includes chips designed for specific AI tasks, such as running trained models.Huawei, T-Head, Kunlunxin and Cambricon together accounted for 95% of the non-GPU segment, which IDC said was being adopted by government agencies, internet companies and telecoms providers.IDC said competition was shifting from the performance of a single chip to system-level capabilities, including how well chips work in a larger computing cluster.IDC expects total accelerator shipments in China to grow 19% this year, even as GPU shipments fall 9%.

title: Most trustworthy AI system demands least inherent model trust, says Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella
title_bn: Most trustworthy AI system demands least inherent model trust, says Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella
author: TechPulse
excerpt: he most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one powered by the model users trust the most, but rather the system that allows people to trust the model the least, Microsoft Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella stated in a post on X.
paragraph1: he most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one powered by the model users trust the most, but rather the system that allows people to trust the model the least, Microsoft Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella stated in a post on X.Most trustworthy AI system demands least inherent model trust, says Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella New Delhi [India], October 11 (ANI): The most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one powered by the model users trust the most, but rather the system that allows people to trust the model the least, Microsoft Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella said.“The most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one with the model we trust most. It will be the one that enables us to trust the model the least,” he said in a post on X..Addressing the governance challenges of advanced artificial intelligence, Nadella noted that modern systems lack the mechanistic clarity of legacy computing.
paragraph2: While engineers once traced software operations directly to specific code paths, such visibility is missing in contemporary frontier architectures.“As traditional software systems were being deployed across the economy over the last few decades, we had the tools and capability to trace behaviors to a specific code path,” Nadella stated.“That same kind of mechanistic understanding eludes us in today’s Super Intelligence systems, even as the frontier models powering these systems are now more capable than traditional software systems. We can’t attribute model behaviors and outputs to specific inputs of training data or configurations of model weights. And yet we are deploying these complex agentic systems and models, with access to our most sensitive data and giving them the ability to take mission-critical actions on our behalf!
paragraph3: ” he said.Nadella warned against relying solely on assurances from developers or treating these deployments as nested black boxes. He emphasized that enterprises cannot outsource responsibility for automated actions and must separate the supply of raw intelligence from ultimate operational authority.“Setting aside the hard problem of alignment, we need to start with an engineering approach to containment and governance. We need to surround non-deterministic models with strong, deterministic system design, human controls, and reliable operating procedures, and establish industry standards where existing ones are insufficient,” Nadella explained.
paragraph4: To manage these risks, Nadella proposed treating both closed and open-weight models as potential insider threats. Because any privileged actor can fail or face compromise, organizations must isolate the models through proven enterprise security practices, such as identity controls, activity logging, and strict permission boundaries.“It’s why the controls that govern what a model can access and what actions it can take must sit outside the model. This builds on an information security principle dating back to the 1970s that a program must not be able to bypass or tamper with the mechanisms that enforce its permissions,” he observed.“Today this means separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work, as well as the action space that defines what it can do.
paragraph5: It also means externalizing controls and safeguards,” Nadella added.Nadella outlined key principles for observing and governing these networks, including model diversity, tamper-proof logging, continuous verifiability across edge cases, independent audits, reliable containment shutoffs, and industrywide incident disclosure.

Because any privileged actor can fail or face compromise, organizations must isolate the models through proven enterprise security practices, such as identity controls, activity logging, and strict permission boundaries.“It’s why the controls that govern what a model can access and what actions it can take must sit outside the model. This builds on an information security principle dating back to the 1970s that a program must not be able to bypass or tamper with the mechanisms that enforce its permissions,” he observed.“Today this means separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work, as well as the action space that defines what it can do.
bangla_paragraph5: It also means externalizing controls and safeguards,” Nadella added.Nadella outlined key principles for observing and governing these networks, including model diversity, tamper-proof logging, continuous verifiability across edge cases, independent audits, reliable containment shutoffs, and industrywide incident disclosure.

title: SoftBank seeks $100 billion for AI-refined projects from Middle Eastern investors
title_bn: SoftBank seeks $100 billion for AI-refined projects from Middle Eastern investors
author: TechPulse
excerpt: SoftBank plans to buy companies that do not use AI or robotics, then apply new technologies to improve their operations and valuation.
paragraph1: Masayoshi Son, founder of SoftBank, is seeking up to $100 billion from Gulf investors to establish a fund that would acquire companies and improve their operations using artificial intelligence and robotics, according to the Financial Times.
paragraph2: The initiative comes as SoftBank faces growing concerns over its $65 billion investment in OpenAI and its delayed initial public offering (IPO).
paragraph3: Unlike SoftBank's previous investment vehicles, which primarily financed technology companies, the proposed fund would purchase established businesses and introduce AI and other advanced technologies to improve their operations in a bid to improve their value, which is a relatively novel model to make money on AI.
paragraph4: Son has reportedly approached influential investors in the Middle East, including senior figures in the United Arab Emirates, in recent weeks to get the money to acquire companies that have not yet adopted AI and/or robotics, but which could substantially improve their business positions by doing so.

title: Super Micro smuggling co-conspirator pleads guilty to sending AI chips to China
title_bn: Super Micro smuggling co-conspirator pleads guilty to sending AI chips to China
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun, one of the three people charged of smuggling Super Micro servers with advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, has pleaded guilty, with sentencing set for September of next year.
paragraph1: Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, a third-party broker and “fixer” who’s been charged alongside Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw and sales manager Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang for conspiring to unlawfully divert Nvidia AI chips to China, has pleaded guilty to the allegations against him. According to Bloomberg, Sun’s plea comes as part of an agreement with prosecutors, although the details of any possible cooperation arrangement remain undisclosed.
paragraph2: Sun is also expected to be sentenced on Sept. 8, 2027, after entering his plea.
paragraph3: The case against the individuals was revealed earlier this year after it was discovered that they diverted Super Micro servers containing Nvidia chips to China. The three were reported to have sent the servers to a Southeast Asian company, which then proceeded to fake the paperwork and create dummy servers for inspectors.
paragraph4: Workers then used hair dryers to remove the serial numbers on the real servers to transfer them to the dummy server shells to complete the illusion, while the real servers made their way to China. Further investigation revealed that the three used a Thailand-based corporation to receive the servers, which were then delivered to Alibaba, even as the Chinese tech giant denied receiving the banned Nvidia hardware.

paragraph2: These prices won’t last long, so you'll need to act quickly.There are plenty of great deals on FDM and resin 3D printers, including machines you’ll find on our list of best 3D printers.
paragraph3: We're also rounding up deals on filament and resin, so you can stock up now. Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing.

title: New Linux tech compresses memory in RAM, as RAM, for 452x speedup
title_bn: নতুন লিনাক্স প্রযুক্তি 452x স্পিডআপের জন্য RAM-এ মেমরি কম্প্রেস করে।
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The new method allows access using standard memory semantics instead of as a block device, drastically improving performance.
paragraph1: A new compression model, called CRAM, offers a different path to compression that avoids swap entirely by keeping the compressed data in memory, and it offers up to 452x the performance of ZRAM. I was a kid in the 1990s when the idea seemed so simple to me: I can use PKZIP to compress my files, so why can't we do that with RAM?
paragraph2: Indeed, I am not a singular genius, and many other people had the same idea, so memory compression has been a feature of most operating systems for a long time. In Linux, the most popular options are zswap and ZRAM, but both of these options are fundamentally swap-layer features.
paragraph3: CRAM is a new take that claims to boost performance tremendously.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
bangla_paragraph1: একটি নতুন কম্প্রেশন মডেল, যাকে সিআরএএম বলা হয়, কম্প্রেশনের জন্য একটি ভিন্ন পথ প্রদান করে যা কম্প্রেস করা ডেটাকে মেমরিতে রেখে সম্পূর্ণরূপে সুপ এড়ায় এবং এটি জেডআরএমের 452x পর্যন্ত পারফরম্যান্স সরবরাহ করে। আমি 1990 এর দশকে একটি শিশু ছিলাম যখন ধারণাটি আমার কাছে এত সহজ মনে হয়েছিলঃ আমি আমার ফাইলগুলি সংকুচিত করতে পিকেজিআইপি ব্যবহার করতে পারি, তাই কেন আমরা এটি র্যাম দিয়ে করতে পারি না?
bangla_paragraph2: প্রকৃতপক্ষে, আমি একক প্রতিভা নই, এবং অনেক অন্য ব্যক্তির একই ধারণা ছিল, তাই মেমরি সংকোচন দীর্ঘদিন ধরে বেশিরভাগ অপারেটিং সিস্টেমের একটি বৈশিষ্ট্য ছিল। লিনাক্সে, সর্বাধিক জনপ্রিয় বিকল্পগুলি হল zswap এবং ZRAM, তবে এই উভয় বিকল্পই মূলত সুইপ-লেয়ার বৈশিষ্ট্য।

title: Exclusive: Swish Pilots Swish Go To Take On Swiggy, Zomato
title_bn: একচেটিয়াঃ সুইশ পাইলট সুইস সুইগির বিরুদ্ধে, জোমাতোর বিরুদ্ধে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Quick food delivery startup Swish seems to be expanding its food delivery offerings with the launch of a new feature…
paragraph1: SUMMARYSwish Go is a new feature offering food delivery for orders sourced from external third-party restaurants and cloud kitchens With this, Swish is diverging from its full-stack model where customers ordered only from its own kitchens The new service, which is being advertised as an offering with no packaging and platform fees, appears to be positioned as a competitor to Swiggy’s Toing and Rapido’s Ownly Quick food delivery startup Swish seems to be expanding its food delivery offerings with the launch of a new feature on its app, Swish Go. Under this, Swish is piloting food delivery for orders sourced from external third-party restaurants and cloud kitchens. This is a model similar to conventional food delivery businesses like Zomato and Swiggy. The new service is being piloted in select pincodes in Bengaluru and is being advertised as an offering with no packaging and platform fees.
paragraph2: Swish has onboarded QSR brands like Nothing Before Coffee, Mealy, Taaka Chinese, among others, for Go. Its positioning appears to put it in direct competition with Swiggy’s Toing and mobility startup Rapido’s Ownly, both of which are also betting on making online food delivery more affordable. This is a divergence for the two-year old startup from its full-stack model where customers ordered only from kitchens owned and operated by the startup. Swish Go also does not promise the 15-minute fulfilment offered by the core Swish app, with orders on the new service expected to take longer.
paragraph3: Inc42 has reached out to Swish with questions around Swish Go. The story will be updated with their responses. Swish was founded in 2024 by Aniket Shah, Ujjwal Sukheja, and Saran S. It currently operates in nearly 50 pin codes across Bengaluru, Gurugram, Noida, Delhi, and Ghaziabad.
paragraph4: The startup has raised $78 Mn in external funding to date from the likes of Hara Global, Bain Capital Ventures, Accel, Alteria Capital and Stride Ventures. Most recently, it raised $24 Mn in a funding round led by Bertelsmann India Investments. Ultra-fast food delivery has been a tough nut to crack even for major players. Swiggy shut down its 15-minute food delivery app SNACC earlier this year, reportedly over concerns around the economics, while Delhi NCR-based startup Zing shut shop as well, stating that it overestimated demand for its product.
paragraph5: Swish has been betting on its differentiated vertically integrated model to succeed where these others couldn’t. It has now entered another emerging segment with Swish Go by positioning low and transparent pricing as the hook of its new service. This is similar to Rapido’s Ownly, which aimed to capitalise on restaurant owners’ discontent with Swiggy and Zomato’s high take rates by charging zero commissions and passing on the cost savings to the consumer. Following Ownly’s challenge, Swiggy has also sought to expand the food-delivery market with Toing, which focuses on affordability without deep discounting by reducing commissions, delivering orders in batches, and limiting the delivery radius.

title: Mukesh Bansal, Ankit Nagori Seek ESOP Buyback From Flipkart Amid IPO Uncertainty
title_bn: মুকেশ বানসাল, অঙ্কিত নাগোরি ইএসওপি ফেরত চাইছেন ফ্লিপকার্টের কাছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Former senior Flipkart executives, including Flipkart’s former CEO Mukesh Bansal, former CFO Sanjay Baweja and former chief business officer Ankit…
paragraph1: SUMMARYGrowth stage funding jumped 46% to $1.1 Bn in Q3 2026, while late stage funding slipped 1% to $994 Mn. A growing pool of early stage capital is supporting Series A and B startups, but late stage funding remains constrained by limited large ticket investors and slower global capital deployment. AI, cleantech and deeptech led Q3 funding, while late stage investors are demanding stronger fundamentals, clearer exit visibility and more realistic valuations. Former senior Flipkart executives, including Flipkart’s former CEO Mukesh Bansal, former CFO Sanjay Baweja and former chief business officer Ankit Nagori, have reportedly urged Walmart to buyback their vested employee stock options (ESOPs) amid uncertainty over the ecommerce major’s public listing plans. The group is said to have written to Walmart’s board, which includes Flipkart group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy, urging for a complete exit opportunity. “This is not merely a request for goodwill.
paragraph2: We contributed our time, effort, expertise and commitment to building the business and creating the value that exists today,” the letter read, as per a report by ET. Demanding a “fair treatment” towards the vested stock options granted to them 10-15 years ago, the ex-Flipkart heads argued that former employees should not be disadvantaged simply because they are no longer on Flipkart’s payroll. The push comes months after Walmart conducted the second tranche of Flipkart’s employee stock buyback programme. The July transaction reportedly valued Flipkart at around $38.2 Bn, but eligible employees could liquidate only up to 5% of their vested options. A Walmart spokesperson said that the company would examine the issues raised by the former executives. “We appreciate the perspective of all employees—current and former—and value their feedback.
paragraph3: As with anything raised, we take it seriously and look into the matter.” “As we’ve said, an IPO remains an active part of our strategic roadmap, and we will move forward when the timing is right. Transitioning to public markets brings great opportunities, but also real operational responsibility. A thoughtful and disciplined approach will help support a successful transition to public markets,” the statement added. Inc42 has reached out to Flipkart, Walmart, Mukesh Bansal, and Sanjay Baweja for comments on the matter. The emails had not received a response at the time of publishing. The story will be updated upon receiving a response.
paragraph4: Flipkart Defers IPO Amid Profitability Push At the heart of the matter is Flipkart’s deferred plans as parent Walmart seeks a valuation of $50 Bn for the ecommerce giant. While the company has reverse flipped to India in a bid to list on the domestic bourses, it doesn’t have a concrete timeline for its public market debut. As of now, the company is said to have deferred the IPO till 2028 as it focuses on enhancing its bottom line. Flipkart is targeting breakeven at an EBITDA level by FY27. Flipkart is currently doubling down on its quick commerce vertical, Flipkart Minutes, with projections of it doubling its dark store count to 2,000 by mid-2027. It is also looking to enter new businesses like food delivery and event ticketing in the near future. The company is yet to disclose its financial performance for the fiscal year FY26.
paragraph5: For the fiscal year FY25, Flipkart Internet, the group’s marketplace arm, reported a 36.7% decline in consolidated net loss to ₹1,494.2 Cr in FY25, while total income increased 14% YoY to ₹20,807.4 Cr.
bangla_paragraph1: সারসংক্ষেপ২০২৬ সালের তৃতীয় প্রান্তিকে বৃদ্ধির পর্যায়ে তহবিল ৪৬% বেড়ে ১.১ বিলিয়ন ডলার হয়েছে, যখন শেষ পর্যায়ে অর্থায়ন ১% হ্রাস পেয়ে ৯৯৪ মিলিয়ন ডলার হয়ে গেছে। একটি ক্রমবর্ধমান প্রাথমিক পর্যায়ে মূলধন সিরিজ এ এবং বি স্টার্টআপগুলিকে সমর্থন করছে, তবে শেষ পর্যায়ের তহবিলে সীমিত বড় টিকিট বিনিয়োগকারী এবং ধীর বিশ্বব্যাপী মূলধনের মোতায়েন দ্বারা সীমাবদ্ধ রয়েছে। এআই, ক্লিনটেক এবং ডিপটেক তৃতীয় প্রতীক তহবিলার নেতৃত্ব দিয়েছে, যখন পরবর্তী পর্যায়ে বিনিয়োগকারীরা শক্তিশালী মৌলিক, আরও স্পষ্ট প্রস্থান দৃশ্যমানতা এবং আরও বাস্তবসম্মত মূল্যায়ন দাবি করছে। প্রাক্তন সিনিয়র ফ্লিপকার্ট নির্বাহীরা, i
bangla_paragraph2: ইটি-র এক প্রতিবেদনে বলা হয়েছে, আমরা আমাদের সময়, প্রচেষ্টা, দক্ষতা এবং আজ বিদ্যমান মূল্য তৈরিতে আমাদের অঙ্গীকারকে অবদান রেখেছি। ১০-১৫ বছর আগে তাদের দেওয়া ন্যস্ত স্টক বিকল্পগুলির প্রতি "ন্যায়সঙ্গত আচরণ" দাবি করে প্রাক্তন ফ্লিপকার্ট প্রধানরা যুক্তি দিয়েছিলেন যে প্রাক্তনের কর্মচারীদের কেবলমাত্র তারা আর ফ্লিपকার্টের বেতনে নেই বলেই ক্ষতিগ্রস্থ করা উচিত নয়।
bangla_paragraph3: "আমরা এই বিষয়ে গুরুত্বের সাথে চিন্তাভাবনা করছি এবং বিষয়টি নিয়ে তদন্ত করছি। যেমনটি আমরা বলেছি, আইপিও আমাদের কৌশলগত রোডম্যাপের একটি সক্রিয় অংশ হিসাবে রয়ে গেছে এবং সঠিক সময় যখন আসবে তখন আমরা এগিয়ে যাব। পাবলিক মার্কেটে রূপান্তরিত হওয়া দুর্দান্ত সুযোগ নিয়ে আসে, তবে বাস্তব অপারেশনাল দায়িত্বও নিয়ে আসে। একটি চিন্তাশীল এবং শৃঙ্খলাবদ্ধ পদ্ধতির মাধ্যমে পাবলিক বাজারে সফল রূপান্তরের জন্য সহায়তা করা হবে", বিবৃতিতে যোগ করা হয়েছে।
bangla_paragraph4: ফ্লিপকার্ট মুনাফা অর্জনের জন্য আইপিও স্থগিত করেছে বিষয়টির কেন্দ্রবিন্দুতে ফ্লিपকার্টের স্থগীত পরিকল্পনা রয়েছে কারণ প্যারেন্ট ওয়ালমার্ট ইকমার্স জায়ান্টের জন্য 50 বিলিয়ন ডলার মূল্যায়ন চায়। যদিও সংস্থাটি দেশীয় এক্সচেঞ্জে তালিকাভুক্ত হওয়ার জন্য ভারতে বিপরীতমুখী হয়েছে, তবে এর পাবলিক মার্কেটে আত্মপ্রকাশের জন্য এর নির্দিষ্ট সময়সীমা নেই। এখন পর্যন্ত বলা হচ্ছে যে সংস্থাটি ২০২৮ সাল পর্যন্ত আইপিओ স্থগিতাদেশ করেছে কারণ এটি তার নীচের লাইনে উন্নতি করতে মনোনিবেশ করেছে। ফ্লিপের্ট ২৭ অর্থবছরের মধ্যে ইবিআইটিডিএ স্তরে ব্রেক ইভেন লক্ষ্য করছে।
bangla_paragraph5: আর্থিক বছর ২৫-এ ফ্লিপকার্ট ইন্টারনেট গ্রুপের মার্কেটপ্লেস বাহিনী ৩৬.৭ শতাংশ হ্রাস পেয়ে ১,৪৯৪.২ কোটি টাকা হয়েছে।

title: Apple to hold event on October 13? New Smart Home Hub, HomePod Mini and Apple TV expected
title_bn: অ্যাপল ১৩ অক্টোবর ইভেন্ট করবে? নতুন স্মার্ট হোম হাব, হোমপড মিনি এবং অ্যাপল টিভি প্রত্যাশিত
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple is expected to announce another batch of products in the final week of October, shortly after a reported smart home product launch around October 13.
paragraph1: Apple is expected to announce another batch of products in the final week of October, shortly after a reported smart home product launch around October 13.Apple may announce new MacBook Ultra, M6 MacBook Pro and iMac in final week of October. (AP)Apple could have a packed October ahead, with reports suggesting that the company is preparing two separate product launches this month.According to MacRumors, Apple is expected to announce another batch of products in the final week of October, shortly after a reported smart home product launch around October 13. Apple has yet to officially confirm either the products or the launch dates.Apple may unveil smart home products firstBloomberg's Mark Gurman has also reported that Apple could launch a new smart home hub featuring a display, an upgraded HomePod mini and a new Apple TV 4K on October 13.It is not yet known whether Apple will host a dedicated event for the launches or reveal the products through videos and press releases. The company has previously used both methods for product announcements.New MacBook models could followThe second round of announcements could include several Mac models that have been the subject of speculation.Among the products reportedly being considered are the long-rumoured MacBook Ultra models. These devices are expected to feature OLED displays along with a thinner and lighter design.Apple could also unveil a 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by the M6 chip, alongside a new iMac featuring the same processor.
paragraph2: Mac Studio launch expected later this monthApple has already confirmed that a high-end Mac Studio equipped with the M5 Ultra chip and up to 512GB of RAM will arrive in late October.However, it remains uncertain whether the Mac Studio will be included in the reported final-week product announcements or launched separately.New iPad mini launch date remains unclearThe new iPad mini is another device that could make an appearance this month. The tablet could be announced alongside the reported smart home products, included in the final week of October launches or unveiled independently at a later date.The device is reportedly set to feature an OLED display, an A20 Pro chip, a landscape-orientated front camera and a redesigned speaker system.Apple already has another major launch plannedThe reported October announcements come as Apple prepares for another major product release. The company is also getting ready to put the iPhone Duo on sale on October 23.With several products potentially arriving within weeks of each other, October could become one of Apple's busiest launch periods this year.iPhone Duo price in IndiaMeanwhile, the Apple iPhone Duo is priced at ₹299,900 for the 256GB model. The 512GB version costs ₹324,900, while the 1TB variant costs ₹374,900.The 2TB version is the highest-end one and comes with an ₹449,900 price tag. All prices are inclusive of taxes and represent the maximum retail price.
paragraph3: Apple iPhone Duo display and designThe iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch inner Super Retina XDR display with nano-texture. Apple says it is 50% bigger than the iPhone 18 Pro Max's screen.Folded, users can enjoy a 5.4-inch Super Retina XDR outer display. Both screens support ProMotion, always-on functionality and up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness.The phone features a Grade 5 titanium frame with Ceramic Shield protection on the front and back. bangla_paragraph1: অ্যাপল অক্টোবরের শেষ সপ্তাহে স্মার্ট হোম পণ্য লঞ্চের পর অল্প সময়ের মধ্যে, অক্টোবরে আরেকটি পণ্য ল্যান্ডিং ঘোষণা করবে বলে আশা করা হচ্ছে।অক্টোবরের চূড়ান্ত সপ্তাহে অ্যাপল নতুন ম্যাকবুক আল্ট্রা, এম 6 ম্যাকবুক প্রো এবং আইম্যাক ঘোষণা করতে পারে। (এপি)অ্যাপল সামনে একটি প্যাকড অক্টোবর থাকতে পারে, রিপোর্টগুলি পরামর্শ দেয় যে সংস্থাটি এই মাসে দুটি পৃথক পণ্য লন্ডারিংয়ের প্রস্তুতি নিচ্ছে।ম্যাকরুমারস অনুসারে, অ্যাপল শীঘ্রই অক্টোবারের শেষ সপ্তাহে পণ্যগুলির আরেকটি ব্যাচ ঘোষণা করবে।
bangla_paragraph2: ম্যাক স্টুডিওর লঞ্চ এই মাসের শেষের দিকে প্রত্যাশিতঅ্যাপল ইতিমধ্যে নিশ্চিত করেছে যে এম 5 আল্ট্রা চিপ এবং 512 গিগাবাইট পর্যন্ত র্যাম দিয়ে সজ্জিত একটি উচ্চ-শেষ ম্যাক স্টুডিও অক্টোবরের শেষের মধ্যে আসবে।যদিও, ম্যাক অ্যাক স্টোরিওটি গত সপ্তাহের পণ্য ঘোষণায় অন্তর্ভুক্ত হবে কিনা বা আলাদাভাবে চালু হবে কিনা তা অনিশ্চিত।নতুন আইপ্যাড মিনি লঞ্চের তারিখ এখনও অস্পষ্ট।নতুনা আইপ্য্যাড মিনী হ'ল আরেকটি ডিভাইস যা এই মাসে উপস্থিত হতে পারে। ট্যাবলেটটি রিপোর্ট করা স্মার্ট এর পাশাপাশি ঘোষণা করা যেতে পারে।
bangla_paragraph3: অ্যাপল আইফোন ডুও প্রদর্শন এবং নকশাআইফোন ড্যুও একটি ন্যানো টেক্সচার সহ 7.6 ইঞ্চি অভ্যন্তরীণ সুপার রেটিনা এক্সডিআর ডিসপ্লে বৈশিষ্ট্যযুক্ত। অ্যাপল বলেছে যে এটি আইফোন 18 প্রো ম্যাক্সের স্ক্রিনের চেয়ে 50% বড়। ভাঁজ করা হলে ব্যবহারকারীরা একটি 5.4-ইঞ্চি সুপার রিটিনা XDR বাইরের ডিসফার উপভোগ করতে পারবেন। উভয় স্ক্রীন প্রোমোশন, সর্বদা-অন কার্যকারিতা এবং 3,000 নিট পর্যন্ত শীর্ষ উজ্জ্বলতা সমর্থন করে। ফোনটিতে সামনের এবং পিছনের দিকে সিরামিক শিল্ড সুরক্ষা সহ গ্রেড 5 টাইটানিয়াম ফ্রেম রয়েছে। এটি আইপি 68 রেটিন সহ জল এবং ধুলো প্রতিরোধী।
bangla_paragraph4: ২. ব্যক্তিগত অর্থঃ মিউচুয়াল ফান্ড, পিপিএফ, এসএসওয়াই, পোস্ট অফিস সঞ্চয়ী প্রকল্প, স্টক টু ওয়াচ, ব্যক্তিগত ঋণ, ক্রেডিট কার্ড, শীর্ষ ব্যাংকের এফডি, রিয়েল এস্টেট, আয়কর এবং আরও অনেক কিছু সম্পর্কে অন্তর্দৃষ্টি। ৩. রাজনীতিঃ সাধারণ নির্বাচন, রাজ্য নির্বাচন এবং উপনির্বাচন, লোকসভা, বিধানসভা , সংসদ, পিএমও, পিআইবি, অর্থ মন্ত্রক, স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রক এবং অন্যান্য কেন্দ্রীয় মন্ত্রক ও সরকারী বিভাগগুলির মধ্যে ব্যাপক কভারেজ। ৪. জাতীয় সংবাদঃ দিল্লি, মুম্বাই এবং ই-এর মতো মেট্রো শহর থেকে ইউ
bangla_paragraph5: সুগম সিংহাল, সিনিয়র সহকারী সম্পাদক ৩. চঞ্চল, সহকারী লেখক ৪. সঞ্চারি ঘোষ, প্রধান সামগ্রী প্রযোজক ৫. প্রতীক প্রশান্ত মুকেন, প্রধান বিষয়বস্তু প্রযাজক ৬. সায়ান্তানি বিশবাস, প্রধান কন্টেন্ট প্রযୋଜক ৭. রবি হরি, উপ-প্রধান সামগ্রী নির্মাতা ৮. গারভিৎ ভিরানি, উপ প্রধান সামগ্ৰী প্রযজ্যক ৯. আকৃতি আনন্দ, সিনেয়র সামগ্রী প্রস্তুতকারক ১০. জসলিন ফেলিক্স ফার্নান্দেস, সিনিয়র সামগ্ৰী প্রস্তুতকারকের ১১. স্বস্তিকা দাস শর্মা, সামগ্রী উৎপাদনকারী ১২. মৌসাম ঝা, সামগ্ৰী উৎপাদনকারী ১৩।
